Path: Scripts/Scenes/Battle/. The engine ships four: scene_battle.lua, scene_battle_init.lua, scene_battle_template.lua, scene_battle_ow.lua; just copy one and modify it.

docs.title: Scene Skeleton
docs.text:
local scene = {}

-- 1) Import the battle module
Battle = ImportFile("Battle")
Battle.SetEndRoom("scene_end")

-- 2) Load the encounter file
Game = Battle.SetGame("Poseur")
Game:AddItem({id = "STABLE", _color = {0.5, 0, 0}, name = "ImNotFood"})

-- 3) Initialize each enemy's animation (one line per enemy)
--    position is just a plain field on the instance; animation ops are also
--    written directly on the instance (dot, no self passed)
Game:InitAnimation(1, {320, 140})

-- Example: after getting the instance, change expression / move position
-- local boss = Game.enemies[1].animation
-- boss.SetFace(3)
-- boss.cpos[1] = 260

-- 4) Write callbacks
local function HandleItems(item)
    Player.Heal(99, true)
    Battle.BattleDialogue({"* You ate " .. item.name .. "."}, "ACTIONSELECT")
end

Battle.HandleItems = HandleItems

-- 5) Background
local background = Sprites.CreateSprite("px.png", "Background")
background:Scale(640, 480)

function scene.update(dt)
    Battle.Update(dt)
end

function scene.clear()
    Layers.clear()
    Battle.Clear()
end

return scene

Neither Line in scene.clear Can Be Omitted

Battle.Clear() clears the whole set of caches — encounter, animation, wave, Soul, attack pattern; Layers.clear() clears the layers. Omit the former and the second time you enter battle you'll get the leftover state from the previous one (enemies still carrying the last HP bar, Soul reusing the last color), and it won't error — very hard to debug.

docs.title: Callback Overview
docs.text:
These callbacks are all fields on Battle, called by the engine at fixed moments. Just override them in the scene; if not written, the engine's empty implementation is used.

Flow Callbacks

  • Battle.HandleActions(enemy, action) The player confirmed an action in ACTMENU.
    • enemy The enemy being acted upon.
    • action The selected action table, containing id and name.
  • Battle.HandleItems(item) The player used an item.
    • item The used item table. Whether the item is consumed is handled by the engine (_cantdestroy = true keeps it).
  • Battle.HandleSpare() The player selected Spare in MERCYMENU, and there are still enemies on the field that haven't been spared.
    • Spareable enemies have already been removed at this point, and their gold has been settled into Battle.GOLD.
    • When not a single enemy remains, the engine goes straight to Battle.Win() and won't reach here; so this callback only appears in scenes where "some enemies are spareable".
  • Battle.HandleFlee() The player selected Flee in MERCYMENU and the check succeeded.
  • Battle.FleeUpdate(dt) Called every frame while in the FLEEING state.
  • Battle.DefenseEnding() Called at the instant the enemy turn ends and returns to the player turn.
  • Battle.OnHit(bullet) The player's Soul touched a bullet.
    • bullet The sprite object hit; read its HurtMode to decide whether to deduct HP.
  • Battle.EnteringState(old, new) Called when the state switches. When overriding, you must call the default implementation first: 
    local function EnteringState(oldstate, newstate)
    Battle.defaultEnteringState(oldstate, newstate)
    -- your own logic
end
  • Battle.Win(extra_texts, on_complete) Battle won. Also recommended to call Battle.defaultWin: 
    local function Win()
    Battle.defaultWin({"* Your LOVE increased!"})
end
Battle.Win = Win

HandleSpare Is an Empty Function in the Engine; Not Taking It Over Causes Trouble

On the engine side there is only function battle.HandleSpare() end. And on the same frame the player confirms Spare, the engine has already destroy_elements() and cleared the Spare menu's options (state.typers). If you do nothing and the state is still stuck at MERCYMENU, the next frame it will read that already-emptied table and directly throw attempt to index a nil value.

So whenever your battle has a situation where "some enemies are spareable, others aren't", you must take it over in the scene. The laziest approach is to just advance to the enemy turn as usual:

local function HandleSpare()
    Battle.BattleDialogue({"* The remaining enemies aren't about to let you off."}, "DEFENDING")
end

Battle.HandleSpare = HandleSpare

The two built-in Poseurs are both canspare = true; one Spare clears them and goes straight to Win(), so you won't hit this in the demo scene.

Standard OnHit

The engine passes the bullet's HurtMode to you as-is; how to interpret it is up to you: The engine passes the bullet's HurtMode to you as-is; how to interpret it is up to you:

local function OnHit(bullet)
    local damage = 1
    local mode = (bullet["HurtMode"] or "normal"):lower()

    if (mode == "normal") then
        Player.Hurt(damage)
    elseif (mode == "blue" or mode == "cyan") then
        -- Blue: only hurt while moving
        if (Controller.GetState("arrows") > 0) then
            Player.Hurt(damage)
        end
    elseif (mode == "orange") then
        -- Orange: only hurt while standing still
        if (Controller.GetState("arrows") <= 0) then
            Player.Hurt(damage)
        end
    end
end

docs.title: Dialogue
docs.text:
Almost all battle text goes through the typewriter; the engine provides two wrappers:

Dialogue Methods

  • Battle.BattleDialogue(texts, final_state) Play a narration; after it finishes, switch to the specified state.
    • texts The text array (cannot be Chinese unless the font supports it).
    • final_state Which state to switch to after playing, default "ACTIONSELECT".
  • Battle.FullDialogue(texts, call) Play a narration; after it finishes, execute a function.
    • call What to do after playing, e.g. function () Battle._end = true end.
  • Battle.narration_text The typewriter object for the always-on narration line in the battle box.

Waiting and Fast-Forwarding in Battle Text

You can mix in typewriter tags within texts; the two most common in battle dialogue are:

  • [wait:x] Pause for x seconds before continuing. It uses the typewriter's own waittime timer, independent of the per-character interval — writing [wait:0.5] then [speed:0.01], that half-second pause won't be swallowed by the speed-up.
  • [speed:x] Change the per-character interval (each character x seconds); takes effect until the next [speed:]. Default 1/15 ≈ 0.0667 seconds.

When the player holds the cancel key (default X), the engine will directly clear the current waittime and immediately finish the remaining characters, without waiting segment by segment. Text with [noskip] ignores this.

The complete tag table is in Basic Development → Typewriter.

docs.title: State and Flow Control
docs.text:
State Methods

  • Battle.ChangeState(new_state) Switch state. This is the only proper way to switch, it guarantees EnteringState is called exactly once.
  • Battle.state The current state. Available values see UI → State Flow.
  • Battle.game The current encounter table.
  • Battle.EXP / Battle.GOLD The EXP and gold accumulated in this battle, auto-added when an enemy dies.
  • Battle._end Once set to true, the screen starts fading out; once the fade completes, it switches to Battle.room_end.
  • Battle.SetEndRoom(room) Set which scene to go to after the battle ends, default "scene_end".
  • Battle.room_end The currently set ending scene name.

Selected Items

  • Battle.selected_enemy_index Which enemy the player currently has selected.
  • Battle.selected_action_index Which action the player currently has selected.
  • Battle.selected_index Which item the player currently has selected.

These three values are especially useful inside EnteringState — e.g. to judge "the player used Check on enemy #1".

docs.title: Other Available Methods
docs.text:
General Methods

  • Battle.Update(dt) Called every frame; advances the player, battle box, UI, and all enemy animations.
  • Battle.UpdateRestore(dt) Called during the battle box's rebound after the enemy turn ends; the engine has already hooked it up.
  • Battle.Clear() Clear the entire battle module tree and the Game-area battle content cache.
  • Battle.SetGame(file) Load the encounter file, returns the encounter table (returns nothing if not found).
  • Battle.SetAttackPattern(name) Switch attack pattern, see Attack Pattern.
  • Battle.Defending() Manually enter the enemy turn (rarely needed; the state machine walks there itself).

docs.title: Connecting with Overworld
docs.text:
Battles entered by bumping into them from the overworld use scene_battle_ow.lua, which does two extra things compared to a normal battle scene:

  1. Entry: Push DATA.player's save data into Player; the battle uses real HP rather than the template values from the encounter file.
  2. Exit: On scene.clear, write EXP / GOLD / remaining HP back into DATA, and settle level-ups per DATA.lv_data.

To change the level-up rules (e.g. raise the level cap from 20 to 30, change the HP curve per level), go to the lv_data table in Game/Logics/init.lua, see Game Logic and World Rules; to change "how much you get for winning", change the enemy's exp and gold in the encounter file.

docs.title: Debugging Tips
docs.text:
• Enemy animation didn't show → check the terminal for [Game - Animation] WARNING: Enemy #x has no animation., most likely the InitAnimation index is wrong.
  • Wave didn't take effect → check for exists but failed to load, see Battle Initialization.
  • Second time entering battle the state is off → check Battle.Clear() in scene.clear.
  • Battle ended but didn't switch scene → check whether the scene name set by Battle.SetEndRoom actually exists.
  • Collision looks wrong (HP deducted though clearly no contact / no deduction though clearly hit) → press F7 to open the hitbox overlay, or call Battle.ToggleHitboxes(true) in code. When perfect-pixel collision is on, you see the real pixel outline rather than a rectangle, see Basic Development → Sprites → Perfect Pixel Collision.

docs.title: Overworld
docs.text:
Overworld is "the part where you walk around on a map": maps, collision, movement, dialogue, save points, chests, encounters — all here.

Path: Scripts/Libraries/Overworld/. Scene path: Scripts/Scenes/Overworld/, with same-named files also accepting Game/Scenes/Overworld/ override.

These modules are likewise not standalone libraries that run on their own. init.lua handles overall assembly and scheduling; map / char / world / stat / shop / Pages each manage a piece, communicating with each other through DATA and the physics world's collision events.

The Game area concept and resource lookup order that recur throughout this topic are explained in one place: Basic Development → Game Area & Resource Override.

docs.title: How an Overworld Runs
docs.text:
Enter Overworld scene
  ↓
Overworld.Init(map path)
  ├─ Build physics world, register collision callbacks
  ├─ Scan Tiled object layers → generate collision bodies and runtime objects
  ├─ Place player at spawn point (mark)
  └─ Auto-limit camera to the map's actual coverage
  ↓
Each frame Overworld.Update(dt)
  ├─ Menu / map / player / save page / chest page / encounter counting
  └─ Player hits warp / chest / sign / save / trigger → recorded into interactions
  ↓
You read interactions in the scene and decide what to do (dialogue, switch scene, open chest…)

docs.title: Pages in This Topic
docs.text: Page Content Initialization & Scene Skeleton How to write a scene, layers, global variables, DATA 🔧 Map & Object Layers Which layers to build in Tiled, each layer's properties, debugging 🔧 STI & Tilesets Tilesets must be embedded in the map, 20 × 20 tiles, tileset image paths, animated tiles Characters Player sprite, movement, collision body, Frisk Dance Interaction & Dialogue Collision interaction, dialogue, scene switching Menu · Save · Chest Menu, save points, chest page Encounters Step-based encounters, connecting with the battle scene Shop Shop scene, buy/sell settlement, rejection lines, conversation topics & queue

docs.title: A Few Things to Know First
docs.text:
Overworld coordinates are doubled

The map uses 20x20 tiles, drawn at an overall 2× scale. So runtime coordinates = Tiled pixel coordinates × 2: a 20x20 tile occupies 40x40 in the world. The engine already multiplies for you when generating collision bodies, so reading obj.x gives you world coordinates; but remember to multiply by 2 when hardcoding values yourself.

The camera is limited to the map

Overworld.Init automatically scans all non-empty tiles in the map, computes the real coverage, and calls Camera:setBounds. To control it yourself, call Camera:setBounds again after Init to override it.

The camera follows the player by default

Overworld.follow_player defaults to true. Set it to false and the camera stops moving; during cutscenes you can manually push the camera with Camera:setPosition(x, y).

docs.title: Initialization and Scene Skeleton
docs.text:
An Overworld scene is very thin — it only does three things: load the Map, play music, and push Overworld every frame.

Path: Scripts/Scenes/Overworld/. The engine ships scene_sol.lua which you can copy directly.

Like other scenes, Game/Scenes/Overworld/<same_name>.lua will override the engine's version. See Basic Development → Scenes.

docs.title: Minimal Scene
docs.text:
local scene = {}
local ow = ImportFile("Overworld")

ow.Init("Maps/main_scene/sol.lua")
ow.SetMusic("Start.ogg")

function scene.update(dt)
    ow.Update(dt)
end

function scene.draw()
    ow.Draw()
end

function scene.clear()
    ow.Clear()
    Layers.clear()
end

return scene

Both lines in scene.clear are required

What ow.Clear() actually does: Map.Destroy() destroys all collision bodies and sprites of the map → Camera:unBounds() unlocks the camera bounds → clears the module cache of the entire Scripts.Libraries.Overworld tree → Camera:reset(). Layers.clear() clears the layers. Omitting the former will cause leftover state from the previous run when entering the Overworld a second time.

Overworld is also one of the types overrideable in the Game area

Overworld belongs to the Scripts.Libraries.Overworld module tree, and the Game/ area does not override it (the things that can be overridden are Encounter / Animations / Waves / Souls / Sprites / Fonts, etc.). To change Overworld behavior, use a hack script under Game/Hacks/. See Basic Development → Game Area and Asset Override.

World.Destroy() is currently never called

World.Destroy() does exist, but there is no call site anywhere in the library — ow.Clear() goes through Map.Destroy(), and the physics world itself is dropped together with the module cache. When writing your own extensions, don't assume it has already been called.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text:
Overworld automatically creates the following layers when imported; the order is the draw/occlusion order:

Layer Value What goes in it Background -100 Background Map 0 The map itself (drawn by the engine; do not manually put things in here) BelowPlayer 49 Things behind the player that can block them (boxes, signs) Player 50 Player UponPlayer 51 Things in front of the player GUI 80 Dialog boxes, menus, save page TOP 100 Full-screen black overlay (scene transition fade) DEBUG 200 Debug drawing

Objects like boxes and signs that are "sometimes in front, sometimes behind" are automatically switched between BelowPlayer and UponPlayer by the engine every frame based on the player's position — you don't need to worry about it.

docs.title: Loading the Map
docs.text:
Initialization methods

  • Overworld.Init(lua_file) loads a map.
    • lua_file is the path of the map file relative to the project root, e.g. "Maps/main_scene/sol.lua".
  • Overworld.ResolveMapPath(lua_file) returns the actual path that will be handed to STI (Game area takes priority). Usually no need to call manually.
  • Overworld.AutoCameraBounds() recomputes the camera bounds based on the map's actual coverage. Init already calls it once automatically.
  • Overworld.SetMusic(mpath) plays background music; an already-playing track of the same name will not be restarted.

Override rules for the map's Game area: Maps/main_scene/sol.lua first looks for Game/Maps/main_scene/sol.lua, and uses it if present.

When overriding a map, bring its tiles along

STI finds tiles by the map file's relative path (the .lua writes ../images/...). So the Game-area copy of the map must also have the corresponding ../images/ directory tree next to it, otherwise the tiles will be entirely missing.

docs.title: Global Variables
docs.text:
Overworld exports a batch of global variables when imported — use them directly when writing scene logic:

Global What it is Overworld Overworld master control table Map Map module (= Overworld.map) World Physics world (= Map.world) Char Player (= Map.char) Stat Menu Save Save page (= Overworld._pages.save) Chest Chest page (= Overworld._pages.chest) Step Encounter step counter DATA Save data (see below) FLAG = DATA.flags CHEST = DATA.chests ITEMS Item database

There are also two global functions:

Global functions

  • GetRelativePos(x, y) converts "screen coordinates" into "world coordinates that follow the camera". Essential when making your own UI.
  • SpawnBlock(x, y, width, height, thickness) draws a white-bordered black-filled box and returns a block object with Destroy().

docs.title: DATA: Save Data
docs.text:
DATA is the save itself. It comes from Game/Logics/init.lua; if a save exists, the saved copy is used directly.

Below are the engine's default values (the original contents of Game/Logics/init.lua):

logic = {
    time = 0,                  -- playtime (seconds)
    room_name = "--",          -- place name shown at the save point
    room = "Overworld",        -- current scene name
    marker = 2,                -- which mark to use when entering the next map
    position = {0, 0},         -- save position
    direction = "down",        -- save facing
    savedpos = false,          -- whether there is a "load position" pending consumption

    player = {
        name = "Chara", lv = 1,
        maxhp = 20, hp = 20,
        gold = 0, exp = 0,
        atk = 0, watk = 0, def = 0, edef = 0,
        weapon = "stick", armor = "bandage",
        items = {              -- inventory (stores item id strings)
            "ButterscotchPie",
            "PunchCard"
        },
        getcell = false,       -- whether the CELL menu is unlocked
        cells = {              -- phone contacts
            {id = "Toriel_1", name = "Call Mom"},
            -- ...
        }
    },
}

How the player's landing spot is determined (three-step override)

Map.Init writes the player's position three times in a row, each later one overriding the earlier:

  1. First place at the first mark (map.objects.marks[1]);
  2. Then use Overworld.FindObject("mark", DATA.marker) to find the mark whose id equals DATA.marker, and move there if found — if not found, stay at the step-1 position, without error;
  3. Finally, if DATA.savedpos is true, place directly at DATA.position (this is the path used when loading / returning from Battle).

So marker = 2 only matters if this map actually has a mark with id = 2.

Other fields on DATA

  • flags custom switch table, accessed via the global FLAG. Use like FLAG["test_killed"] = 1.
  • chests what is in the chests, accessed via the global CHEST, in the form CHEST["chest"] = {"Spider"}.
  • lv_data level table, 20 levels, each with hp / at / df / totalExp. Both level-up settlement and menu display read from it.

There is a dedicated page for Game/Logics/

World rules (how the level curve is set, how to expand past max level, story switches, chest contents) are all written in Game Logic and World Rules. This page only covers how DATA is used at runtime.

Game/Logics/init.lua is a hard require, with no fallback

The source of DATA is hardcoded to require("Game.Logics") (Scripts/Libraries/Overworld/init.lua line 85). The engine itself does not ship this file, so deleting or renaming it will crash directly. To reset the save, delete the save variable first, not the file.

Changed Logics but nothing took effect?

At the end of Game/Logics/init.lua there is a snippet: if Global.GetSaveVariable("Overworld") exists, the entire logic is replaced with the saved copy — your changed defaults will be completely skipped. When debugging, comment out those two lines, or delete the save variable first.

docs.title: ITEMS: Item Database
docs.text:
The lookup order for the item table is Game.Logics.items → Scripts.Logics.items (the owRequireGameFirst in Scripts/Libraries/Overworld/init.lua).

The Scripts/Logics/ fallback directory does not currently exist

The engine side simply has no Scripts/Logics/items.lua, so that entry in the list can never be hit — in fact the item table only has Game/Logics/items.lua as a source. When both are missing, it prints [Overworld] WARNING: items table not found under Game.Logics or Scripts.Logics., and then any use of ITEMS.FindItemByID will crash from indexing nil.

local db = {
    {id = "MonsterCandy", name = "Monster Candy"},
    {id = "Spider",       name = "Spider", _color = {0.5, 1, 0}},
    -- ...
}

db._actions = {
    {
        id = "Spider",
        use  = {"* You ate the Spider...", "* I CAN'T UNDERSTAND."},
        info = {"* A spider."},
        drop = {"* You dropped the Spider...\n* But nothing happened."}
    }
}

ITEMS methods

  • ITEMS.FindItemByID(id) gets the item definition by id, returning a table with id / name / _color.
  • ITEMS.GetActionByID(id, action) gets a piece of text for an item.
    • action is "use" / "info" / "drop".

The inventory only stores id strings; the name and color are looked up via FindItemByID at display time.

docs.title: Overworld Master Control Method Reference
docs.text:
Overworld methods

  • Overworld.Init(lua_file) loads the map.
  • Overworld.Update(dt) advances every frame (menu → map → save page → chest page → encounter counter).
  • Overworld.Draw() draws; currently an empty implementation, left for you to draw the HUD.
  • Overworld.Clear() destroys everything and clears the cache.
  • Overworld.SetMusic(mpath) plays music.
  • Overworld.CalcNextEXP() returns how much EXP is still needed for the next level.

Overworld properties

  • Overworld.map the map module.
  • Overworld.stat the menu module.
  • Overworld.debug whether debug drawing is enabled, default false.
  • Overworld.follow_player whether the camera auto-follows the player, default true.
  • Overworld.ui_prefer whether the dialog box appears at the top or bottom by default, "down" (default) or "up".

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
Set Overworld.debug to true:

  • All Tiled object collision bodies are drawn (colored by type).
  • Pressing Space teleports the camera to the world coordinate under the mouse, for aligning coordinates.

See Maps and Object Layers → Debug.

docs.title: 🔧 Maps and Object Layers
docs.text:
Maps are edited in Tiled, exported to .lua and placed in Maps/. The engine reads them with the built-in STI library and translates object layers into collision bodies.

Path: Maps/ (engine default), Game/Maps/ (Game area, same-name override). Module path: Scripts/Libraries/Overworld/map.lua, exposed as the global Map.

docs.title: Basic Map Parameters
docs.text:
The engine's built-in maps all use these parameters; copy them when creating a new map:

Item Value Orientation orthogonal Tile size 20 x 20 Map size 30 x 20 (changeable) Export format .lua

The exported .lua goes under Maps/ (or Maps/subdir/). Keeping the Tiled project and .tmx in Maps/tmx/ is just a convention for easily finding and editing them later.

Two more hard constraints on tilesets

Tilesets must be "embedded in the map" (no external .tsx), otherwise STI will directly assert and crash the scene; tile size must be 20 × 20. The tricks around tile image paths and animated tiles are all covered in STI and Tilesets.

docs.title: Object Layers
docs.text:
The name of an object layer determines how it is processed. A misspelled name (or a Chinese name) will cause the entire layer to be ignored.

Layer name Purpose Common properties marks Spawn point / teleport landing id, direction walls Walls (solid collision) id (optional) warps Teleport region (switch scene on contact) id triggers Custom trigger region id + any custom property signs Sign id (optional) saves Save point id, room, x, y chests Chest id, give

These layers fall into three categories, processed differently:

Category Layer Physics body Can the player walk through? Pure data marks none Yes (no collision involved) Solid walls static rectangle / polygon / ellipse No, truly blocks the way Sensor warps, triggers kinematic + setSensor(true) Yes, walking in records it into the interaction list Blocking interactive signs, saves, chests kinematic (not a sensor) No, but contact still records it into the interaction list

In other words, only warps and triggers are "passable regions"; signs, save points, and chests block you just like real walls — you must get up against them to trigger them. These three internally use the same contact event (beginContact), except the collision shape is taken as a narrow strip at the bottom of the sprite.

marks has no physics body

marks is only read as a coordinate point {x, y, direction}, generating no collision body and no sprite. So it can be placed inside a wall, or used as a pure logic anchor.

Coordinates must be multiplied by 2

When reading objects, the engine multiplies x / y / width / height by 2 before building collision bodies. So the coordinates obtained at runtime are already world coordinates, but the numbers you see in Tiled are pre-scale.

docs.title: marks spawn point
docs.text:
Determines where the player stands when entering this map. id is its number, direction is the facing upon entry.

  • Nothing specified → use the first mark.
  • DATA.marker has a value → use the mark matched by id (written by Overworld.ChangeScene when switching scenes).
  • DATA.savedpos is true → use the DATA.position save position (load / return from Battle).

Returning from Battle relies on savedpos

When an encounter triggers, the engine automatically sets DATA.savedpos to true and records the current position, so after the fight the player returns to the original spot instead of the spawn point.

docs.title: walls
docs.text:
walls is the only thing that truly blocks the player. All three shapes are supported:

  • Rectangle (default)
  • Polygon — diagonal walls, sharp corners, anything
  • Ellipse / circle — uses the smaller of width or height as the diameter

The rotation property is applied correctly (both polygons and ellipses rotate along).

Wall friction

Both wall and player friction are 0.01 — deliberately low: with low friction, the player slides along the wall when hitting a diagonal wall instead of sticking to it. The two values are in wall_friction in map.lua and in char.lua respectively; setting them to large numbers makes the player "stick to walls".

docs.title: warps teleport region
docs.text: A region that switches scene on contact. It only tells you that contact happened; the scene-switching action is written by you in the scene script (see Interaction and Dialogue).

docs.title: triggers custom trigger region
docs.text:
Like warps, this is a sensor, but with no fixed purpose — add any properties you like. The most common usage is to add a custom property (e.g. rr) as a "room number" and branch on it.

if (Overworld.getInteractResult("trigger", 1, "rr")) then
    -- touched a trigger region where rr == 1
end

docs.title: signs / saves / chests
docs.text:
The engine automatically generates sprites for these three (sign, save point, chest) — no need to draw them yourself. Properties:

  • signs — if id is left blank, auto-numbered by placement order.
  • saves — room is the place name shown at the save point, x / y are the save coordinates.
  • chests — give is read verbatim into the runtime object's give field (blank = false), but nothing in the engine reads it. What a chest actually gives is decided by CHEST (= DATA.chests) and your scene script. See Menu · Save · Chest.

docs.title: Runtime Access
docs.text:
All objects are collected into Map.objects, tabulated by type:

Object containers

  • Map.objects.marks / .walls / .warps / .triggers / .signs / .saves / .chests are the runtime object lists for each type.
  • Map.objects.unknowns holds object layers whose name didn't match. This table is currently always empty — the engine only dispatches by known layer names, and silently skips unrecognized layers rather than writing to here. Spotting a typo requires Map.debug_objects (see below).
  • Map.debug_objects the raw Tiled objects, indexed by layer name (including misspelled layers), for debug drawing only.

How to find a misspelled layer name

With Overworld.debug on, all object layers in Map.debug_objects are drawn, including the misspelled one. If its name isn't in the color table, it falls into unknowns' dark red — a patch of dark red boxes means this layer's name wasn't recognized by the engine. See "Debug" at the end of this page.

Each runtime object roughly looks like this:

{
    x, y,               -- world coordinates (already ×2)
    width, height,      -- size (already ×2)
    id,                 -- the id in properties
    properties,         -- all properties filled in for this object in Tiled
    body, fixture,      -- physics body (present for walls / warps / triggers / signs / saves / chests)
    sprite,             -- sprite (present for signs / saves / chests)
}

If you don't want to touch collision and just want to fetch an object by condition, Overworld.FindObject is more convenient. See Interaction and Dialogue.

docs.title: Map and Physics World
docs.text:
Map methods

  • Map.Init(lua_file) loads the map. Skips and prints a hint if already initialized.
  • Map.Update(dt) advances tile animation, the physics world, the player, and the camera. Called automatically by the engine.
  • Map.Destroy() destroys all collision bodies and sprites.
  • Map.current the actual path of the current map file (may be the Game-area copy).
  • Map.char the player module.
  • Map.world the physics world.

World methods

  • World.Init() builds the physics world and registers collision callbacks. Repeated calls are ignored.
  • World.Update(dt) advances the physics world.
  • World.Destroy() destroys the physics world and all bodies within it.
  • World.interactions interaction state (see Interaction and Dialogue).

Tile animation needs Update

Tiled's animated tiles only advance when Map.Update calls map:update(dt). This line is already written by the engine — don't delete it while optimizing.

docs.title: Camera
docs.text:
Overworld.Init scans all visible tile layers, computes the rectangle that actually has content (accounting for layer offsets and the negative-coordinate regions of infinite maps), then converts it into Camera:setBounds based on the viewport size.

When the coverage is smaller than the viewport, the camera is locked at the center.

To take manual control:

ow.Init("Maps/main_scene/sol.lua")
Camera:setBounds(min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y)   -- override the automatic result
Camera:setPosition(x, y)                        -- manual positioning
Overworld.follow_player = false                 -- turn off auto-follow

docs.title: Debug
docs.text:
Overworld.debug = true

Once enabled:

  • All object layers' collision bodies are drawn, colored by type (walls red, triggers green, warps magenta, saves yellow, chests orange, signs purple, marks cyan).
  • Press Space to teleport the camera to the mouse position.

docs.title: 🔧 STI and Tilesets
docs.text: Map files are read by the engine's built-in STI (Scripts/Libraries/STI/). It is a general-purpose library, not written for this engine, so there are two hard constraints that must be obeyed — violating them doesn't mean "drawing a bit less", but that the entire Overworld fails to load.

docs.title: Hard Constraint 1: Tilesets must be embedded in the map
docs.text:
When STI loads tilesets, it has this line:

assert(not tileset.filename, "STI does not support external Tilesets.\nYou need to embed all Tilesets.")

In other words: tilesets cannot exist as external .tsx files, they must be embedded in the map.

How to choose in Tiled Exported .lua ✅ Embedded in map Keep the default Embed in map when creating a tileset; for an already-external one, right-click in the tileset panel → Embed Tileset tilesets has no filename ❌ External tileset Checked "Save as external tileset file (.tsx)" when creating One extra line filename = "xxx.tsx"

Hitting this triggers an assert crash

Using an external tileset, the sti(map.current, {"box2d"}) inside Map.Init will directly throw the English error above, interrupting scene loading. It happens the instant you enter the scene, and is easily misdiagnosed as "the map file is broken". How to check: open the exported .lua and search for filename — as long as there is this line in tilesets, it wasn't embedded.

Each map stores its own copy

Embedding applies to a single map, so each .lua repeats a section of tilesets definition. This is a hard requirement of STI that cannot be bypassed; the only cost is a slightly larger export file, and the tile images themselves are not duplicated.

docs.title: Hard Constraint 2: Tiles are 20 × 20
docs.text:
The standard tile size in UNDERTALE is 20 × 20 pixels — copy this when creating a new map:

Item Value Map Tile Size 20 x 20 Tileset Tile Size 20 x 20 Margin / Spacing 0 / 0

The engine draws the map at 2× scale, so:

  • One tile occupies 40 × 40 pixels on a 640 x 480 canvas;
  • One screen shows 16 × 12 cells;
  • The default 30 x 20 cell map = world coordinates 1200 x 800.

Filling it wrong won't error

The engine does not validate this number. Setting tiles to 16 or 32, the game still runs, but the terrain won't align to the grid, and seams or misalignment appear between sprites — very tedious to troubleshoot.

Large decorations can be exceptions

Not every tile needs to be 20 × 20. Whole pieces of furniture like beds and pianos can use a separately-sized tileset (the engine's own Maps/main_scene/main_0.lua has a 50 x 68 bed). But all tiles within the same tileset must be the same size — don't stuff furniture into the terrain tileset.

docs.title: Tile Image Paths
docs.text:
This is how STI assembles the image path:

utils.format_path(path .. tileset.image)   -- path = the directory of the map .lua
  • The path is relative to the map's .lua file, not to the project root.
  • The image is read directly from disk by love.image.newImageData(), not through Sprites' resource resolution.

From this, three rules follow:

Don't export the .lua to another directory

The .tmx and the exported .lua must be placed in the same directory (or at the same relative depth). Exporting to a different directory makes the relative path written by Tiled invalid, manifesting as an entirely empty map with no error at all.

When overriding a map in the Game area, the tile images aren't overridden too

Game/Maps/xxx.lua can override Maps/xxx.lua, but its image is still looked up on the Game/Maps/ side. So when you put a map in the Game area, you must also copy its tile images there at the same relative path.

File names are case-sensitive

Tile image paths are case-sensitive — it runs on Windows, but when packaged to Android / Linux the whole map turns white. Also use only ASCII in paths; avoid Chinese directory names.

docs.title: Animated Tiles
docs.text:
UNDERTALE's water, torches, and waterfalls are all animated tiles. To make an animated tile in Tiled:

  1. Double-click the tileset in the Tilesets panel to open the tileset editor (just selecting it in the map is not enough).
  2. Select the cell to be the animation "host" — this is the cell you paint on the map.
  3. Open the animation editor: menu Tile → Animation (in some versions it's under the Tileset menu; in the Chinese UI it's "Tile → Animation"), or click the film-strip icon on the tileset editor toolbar; a timeline expands below the tileset view.
  4. Drag each frame from the tileset into the timeline; drag to reorder.
  5. Below each frame on the timeline is that frame's duration (milliseconds), which you can click to edit. Tiled previews it looping.
  6. Export the .lua.

After export, that cell gets an extra section in tiles:

tiles = {
  {
    id = 12,
    animation = {
      { duration = 150, tileid = 12 },
      { duration = 150, tileid = 13 },
      { duration = 150, tileid = 14 },
    }
  }
}

No work is needed on the engine side — map.lua's Map.Update already calls map._map:update(dt), and STI will accumulate the time, advance the frame, and push the new frame's quad back into the sprite batch on its own.

STI's advancement logic (STI/init.lua's Map:update) 
tile.time = tile.time + dt * 1000          -- dt is seconds, multiply by 1000 to get milliseconds
while tile.time > tonumber(tile.animation[tile.frame].duration) do
    tile.time  = tile.time - duration
    tile.frame = tile.frame + 1
    if tile.frame > #tile.animation then tile.frame = 1 end
end
-- after advancing the frame: write the new frame's quad back into the sprite batch of all instances
local t = self.tiles[tile.animation[tile.frame].tileid + self.tilesets[tile.tileset].firstgid]
j.batch:set(j.id, t.quad, j.x, j.y, j.r, tile.sx, tile.sy, 0, j.oy)

docs.title: Four pitfalls of animated tiles
docs.text:
Duration unit is milliseconds

The 150 filled in the timeline is 150 milliseconds, not 0.15 nor 150 frames. To make a cell stay for 0.5 seconds, fill in 500.

Animation frames must come from the same tileset

STI computes the frame's gid via tileid + firstgid, and this firstgid comes from the host cell's tileset. Cross-tileset references fetch completely unrelated cells — no error, just weird patterns drawn.

All instances are always in phase

STI advances the animation by tile (gid), not by "each instance placed on the map". So all the same animated tile in one map will play together in sync — you can't get the effect of water flow or flames with staggered phases. To stagger them, copy the frames to make a second animated tile and place them manually offset.

Unused animations cost no performance

Map:update only refreshes the batch when self.tileInstances[tile.gid] exists — i.e. only tiles actually painted on the map go through this. Animations that are defined but never placed won't slow down the frame rate.

Animation is visual only

Animated tiles don't participate in collision and produce no runtime objects — collision is entirely determined by object layers. See Maps and Object Layers.

docs.title: A pit that can ruin the entire map: a leaked setColor
docs.text:
STI draws tiles using lg.setColor(r, g, b, a * layer.opacity) inside Map.drawLayer — in other words, it uses whatever color is currently in the environment.

And LÖVE's default love.run does not reset the drawing state between frames (it only calls origin() and clear()). So:

As long as you setColor in some frame and forget to restore it, that color will leak across frames, becoming the "ambient color" of the next frame, tinting the entire map with color / transparency.

The engine has already handled one real accident, in the virtual keyboard:

-- Scripts/Libraries/Controller/VirtualKeyboard.lua  Draw()  at the end
-- The default love.run does NOT reset the graphics state between frames (it only
-- calls origin() + clear()). The colour left behind here therefore became the
-- ambient colour of the NEXT frame -- and STI paints the tilemap with that
-- ambient colour ... so a leaked tint made every map tile render translucent
-- (once into STI's own map canvas, once again when that canvas is blitted back).
SE.graphics.setColor(1, 1, 1, 1)

Do the same when drawing your own HUD / dialog boxes

The rule is simple: wherever you setColor, restore the color to (1, 1, 1, 1) after drawing. The symptom is "the map suddenly became semi-transparent / turned red", a problem that looks completely unrelated to your code, and is very hard to trace. Same for fonts — restore setFont at frame end too.

docs.title: Character
docs.text:
The little walking person in the Overworld. It is driven by a physics body, followed by a sprite, with the walking animation cycling through sprite frames.

Module path: Scripts/Libraries/Overworld/char.lua, exposed as the global Char.

docs.title: Walking Sprites
docs.text:
One frame group per direction, defaulting to the Frisk set:

Char.sprites = {
    up    = {"Overworld/Frisk/spr_f_maincharau_0.png", ...},
    down  = {"Overworld/Frisk/spr_f_maincharad_0.png", ...},
    left  = {"Overworld/Frisk/spr_f_maincharal_0.png", ...},
    right = {"Overworld/Frisk/spr_f_maincharar_0.png", ...},
}

Sprite methods

  • Char.SetPlayerSprites(tab) replaces the whole group. The table structure must match the above (one array per direction).
  • Char.SetPosition(x, y, direction) sets position and facing. Called automatically by the engine after the map loads.
  • Char.Init() creates the sprite and physics body. Called automatically when the map loads; generally no need to call manually.
  • Char.Destroy() destroys the sprite and physics body.

Swap the protagonist without changing code

These paths are all resolved by Sprites, so they follow the standard Game-area-first rule. To use your own character, drop a same-named file into Game/Resources/Sprites/Overworld/Frisk/ and it will be used automatically, without touching a single line of code (provided the file names and frame counts match). A more thorough approach is Char.SetPlayerSprites{...} inside the scene to switch to another set of paths.

The sprite's anchor point is at the feet, so Char.currentSprite.y is 20 less than the physics body's y (half a body height). Use the sprite coordinate when fetching "where the player's feet are", and use Char.collision.body when fetching "where the collision body is".

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
Char properties

  • currentSprite the current sprite object. nil before the player is spawned, so check for nil before writing scene logic.
  • direction current facing ("up" / "down" / "left" / "right").
  • controlling whether the player can be controlled. Dialogue, menus, and the save page all set this to false.
  • isMoving whether the player actually moved this frame.
  • animationFrame / animationTime walking animation frame number and timer.
  • x / y the spawn (or most recent SetPosition) coordinates.
  • collision.body / .shape / .fixture the physics trio. The collision box is 38 x 20 by default.
  • friskdance whether the Frisk Dance easter egg is enabled (read from the global switch EnableFriskDance).
  • frisk_dancing whether it is currently dancing.

docs.title: Locking Control
docs.text:
All interfaces that "interrupt the player" are implemented via Char.controlling:

Char.controlling = false   -- player stops, no longer reads input
-- ... performance ...
Char.controlling = true    -- resume

Overworld.dialogNew, Save.Show, Chest.Show, and the Stat menu all maintain it themselves, so in normal flow you don't need to worry — unless you wrote something that needs to freeze the player.

Don't forget to unlock

If it's set to false and never restored, the player can never move again, with no error message.

docs.title: Frisk Dance
docs.text:
The original game's easter egg of "press up+down against a wall". The switch is on the global variable EnableFriskDance, which the engine reads into Char.friskdance at startup.

  • Start: facing up, pressed against a wall, holding up+down at the same time.
  • Maintain: keep holding up+down, and the vertical position doesn't move (i.e. still against the wall), and it keeps dancing — sliding left/right doesn't count as interruption.
  • Interrupt: the moment the vertical position moves (walking away from the wall, getting pushed through, falling down…), or releasing up/down, it stops immediately and turns back to facing up.

While dancing, the character toggles between the up / down sprite groups, while still being able to walk left/right.

To turn it off, write in the scene:

Char.friskdance = false

docs.title: How Movement Is Implemented
docs.text:
Char.Update does four things each frame:

  1. Read the four arrow keys, compute the velocity (±2 per frame).
  2. Remember the first direction pressed; it won't be stolen by another direction until released — so to turn around you must release first.
  3. Write the velocity into the physics body and let Box2D handle wall collisions.
  4. Let the sprite follow the physics body and switch walking frames by velocity.

Why you must keep holding up

The engine determines "pressed against a wall" by: the physics body had no vertical displacement this frame. So pushing diagonally doesn't work — you must face the wall head-on first; likewise, the moment the vertical position slides during the dance, the check fails and the easter egg stops. The check has a 0.5-pixel tolerance, so the tiny jitter when against a wall won't falsely break it.

docs.title: Teleporting the Player
docs.text:
Without switching scenes, just move the player:

Char.collision.body:setPosition(x, y)   -- physics body
Char.SetPosition(x, y, "down")          -- sync the record

To switch scenes, use Overworld.ChangeScene. See Interaction and Dialogue.

docs.title: Interaction and Dialogue
docs.text: What happens after the player touches something is entirely decided by your scene script. The engine only tells you "you touched it, and who you touched".

docs.title: How Interactions Arise
docs.text:
The physics world's collision callback records the contacted objects into World.interactions:

interactions fields

  • can_interact whether you are currently touching some interactive object.
  • current_object the type touched ("warp" / "chest" / "sign" / "save" / "trigger").
  • current_id the id of the touched object.
  • current_obj the runtime object actually touched, whose properties you can read.
  • touching the list of all objects currently being touched (possibly more than one).

No need to face it

The check only looks at collision, and does not require the player to face that direction. The original game's "must walk in front of the sign" restriction is not implemented here — touching it counts.

docs.title: Reading Interactions
docs.text:
Reading methods

  • Overworld.getInteractResult(obj_type, id, extra_key) whether you are currently touching something matching the condition.
    • obj_type the type name, e.g. "warp".
    • id if omitted, returns true as long as the type matches.
    • extra_key if omitted (or passed a number), matches by id; if passed a string, matches by that named custom property (e.g. "rr").
    • When matching by property, the value of that property is returned (not true) — if rr is 3, it returns 3, directly usable as a number.
  • Overworld.getTouchResult(obj_type, id, extra_key) same as above, but checks every object in touching rather than only the last one touched.
  • Overworld.FindObject(obj_type, id, extra_key) doesn't require being touched — searches the whole map directly and returns the runtime object table.
    • obj_type is written in singular ("warp" / "mark" / "chest"), internally concatenated into objects["warps"] for lookup.

getTouchResult is not subject to two common protections

Both getInteractResult and onConfirm have two gates: the frame right after a dialog ends returns false directly, and when Char.controlling is false returns nil directly. getTouchResult has neither. It only reads the touching list, so:

  • It still returns true when the player is locked (in dialog / in menu);
  • When using getTouchResult for triggers, it's easy to get "the confirm key that closed the dialog re-opens it". You must add your own deduplication via FLAG, etc.

The 4th parameter of old scripts is ignored

getInteractResult's old signature had a 4th parameter (back then a "must face" switch). It is now accepted but ignored, just so old scene scripts still run. The facing check itself is gone (see above) — don't write it in new code.

Use getTouchResult when overlapping

getInteractResult only looks at "the last one touched". When two trigger regions overlap, the one touched first gets overridden by the one touched later. In cases where hitting any one counts (e.g. "entered a certain room"), always use getTouchResult.

-- touched a warp with id 1
if (Overworld.getInteractResult("warp", 1)) then ... end

-- touched a trigger whose custom property rr equals 1
if (Overworld.getInteractResult("trigger", 1, "rr")) then ... end

-- touching any sign at all
if (Overworld.getInteractResult("sign")) then ... end

docs.title: One-key Confirm
docs.text:
onConfirm merges "touching + pressed confirm" into one call — the most common pattern:

Confirm methods

  • Overworld.onConfirm(type_name, id, sub_key, func) executes func when the condition is met and the confirm key is pressed.
    • sub_key optional; if passed, additionally matches by that custom property.
    • When sub_key is omitted, the third parameter is directly the callback function.
Overworld.onConfirm("sign", 1, function ()
    Overworld.dialogNew({"* ​这是​一块​告示牌​。"})
end)

Overworld.onConfirm("trigger", 1, "rr", function ()
    Overworld.ChangeScene("Overworld.scene_ruins", 2, "down")
end)

docs.title: Dialogue
docs.text:
Dialogue methods

  • Overworld.dialogNew(texts, position) pops up a dialog box and returns the dialog object.
    • texts an array of text.
    • position "down" (bottom of screen, default) or "up" (top).
  • Overworld.ui_prefer the default value used when position is not passed.

The returned dialog has two fields: block (the white-bordered black-filled box) and text (the typewriter object).

The engine destroys the box and unlocks the player by default after the text finishes. To do something more, override text._onComplete:

local dialog = Overworld.dialogNew({"* ​你​捡起​了​一块​石头​。"})

dialog.text._onComplete = function ()
    dialog.block:Destroy()
    Char.controlling = true
    -- your own follow-up logic
end

docs.title: Switching Scenes
docs.text:
Scene-switching methods

  • Overworld.ChangeScene(scene, mark, direction) fades out and switches to another scene.
    • scene the target scene name, e.g. "Overworld.scene_ruins".
    • mark which spawn point of the target map to land on, default 1.
    • direction facing after landing, default "down".

It immediately locks the player and begins fading out, and only actually switches the scene once the black overlay is fully dark. At the same time it writes DATA.room / marker / direction into the save.

Use DATA to pass data across maps

DATA is global when switching scenes and won't be lost; state to carry over (story progress, dropped items, etc.) is written directly into DATA or FLAG.

docs.title: A Complete Scene Script
docs.text:
Putting the parts above together:

local scene = {}
local ow = ImportFile("Overworld")

ow.Init("Maps/main_scene/sol.lua")
ow.SetMusic("Start.ogg")

function scene.update(dt)
    ow.Update(dt)

    -- sign
    ow.onConfirm("sign", 1, function ()
        ow.dialogNew({"* ​欢迎​来到​遗迹​。", "* ​请​小心​脚下​。"})
    end)

    -- save point
    ow.onConfirm("save", 1, function ()
        local save = ow.FindObject("save", 1)
        ow.SaveInteract({"* ​你​感到​了​希望​。"}, "​遗迹​ - ​入口​", save.position, "down")
    end)

    -- chest
    ow.onConfirm("chest", 1, function ()
        ow.ChestInteract("chest")
    end)

    -- warp
    ow.onConfirm("warp", 1, function ()
        ow.ChangeScene("Overworld.scene_ruins", 2, "down")
    end)

    -- custom trigger region: say one line when entered (only once)
    if (ow.getTouchResult("trigger", 1, "rr") and not FLAG["said_hello"]) then
        FLAG["said_hello"] = true
        ow.dialogNew({"* ……​这里​好​安静​。"})
    end
end

function scene.draw()
    ow.Draw()
end

function scene.clear()
    ow.Clear()
    Layers.clear()
end

return scene

docs.title: Common Pitfalls
docs.text:
On the frame right after a dialog ends, getInteractResult always returns false

The engine has a single-frame lock: on the frame the text finishes, all getInteractResult calls return false (getTouchResult is unaffected). This prevents the infinite loop of "the confirm key that closed the dialog immediately re-opens it". If you want to trigger two things in a row on that frame, the second will be swallowed — move it to the next frame, or write your own state machine.

When Char.controlling is false, getInteractResult does nothing

getInteractResult has if (not Char.controlling) then return end (note it returns nil, not false). If you locked the player yourself but forgot to restore it, interactions via getInteractResult / onConfirm will silently fail. But getTouchResult and FindObject don't look at this field — they always work normally.

Make the dialog box follow the camera

When making your own UI, use GetRelativePos(x, y) to convert coordinates; don't write screen coordinates directly — the camera moves.

docs.title: Menu · Save · Chest
docs.text: The Overworld's "pop-up that covers the screen" interfaces are all built by the engine — you only need to call them.

docs.title: Menu Stat
docs.text:
Automatically opened when the player presses the menu key (Controller.GetState("menu")) — no code needed.

Module path: Scripts/Libraries/Overworld/stat.lua, exposed as the global Stat.

Menu methods

  • Stat.Update(dt) called every frame, responsible for opening the menu and processing input. Already wired by the engine.
  • Stat.Destroy() closes the menu and restores player control.
  • Stat._created whether the menu is currently open.
  • Stat._page the current sub-page, a lowercase string: "idle" / "item" / "item2" / "stat" / "cell".
    • "idle" is the state "menu open, cursor on the three big buttons" (corresponding to the ITEM / STAT / CELL layer below);
    • "item2" is the "Use / Info / Drop" three-choice after holding an item in the inventory.

docs.title: Three sub-pages
docs.text:
Page Content Display condition ITEM Inventory (up to 8 slots) Always; text dims when inventory is empty STAT Name, LV, HP, atk/def, weapon/armor, EXP Always CELL Phone contacts (up to 10 slots) Only when DATA.player.getcell is true

The ITEM / STAT / CELL in the table are the names of the three buttons on the interface, not the value of Stat._page — the latter is always lowercase.

After entering ITEM, pressing confirm again goes to the "Use / Info / Drop" three-choice (_page becomes "item2").

To show CELL, set getcell

The third menu item only appears after DATA.player.getcell = true. stat.lua already has DATA.player.getcell = true at the top level; to disable it by default, change it to false.

docs.title: Save Point Save
docs.text:
After touching a save point, just call Overworld.SaveInteract — it plays dialogue first, then opens the save page.

Save methods

  • Overworld.SaveInteract(texts, location, position, direction) plays dialogue and saves.
    • texts what the save point says.
    • location the place name shown on the save screen.
    • position the save coordinates {x, y}, usually taken from the saves object's properties.
    • direction the save facing.
  • Save.Show() opens the save page directly (without dialogue).
  • Save.Hide() closes the save page.
  • Save.Update() processes input, already wired by the engine.
  • Save._active whether the save page is open.

SaveInteract conveniently does three things: fully restores HP, plays snd_heal.wav, and writes DATA.room / room_name / position / direction / savedpos.

The actual save-to-disk happens when the player chooses ​保存​ (Save) on the save page:

Global.SetSaveVariable("Overworld", DATA)

The save is the entire DATA

The save writes the entire DATA table, with no whitelist and no version number. Adding fields to DATA is safe; but renaming a field will make old saves read nil — think it through before release.

docs.title: Chest Chest
docs.text:
A chest is a two-column exchange interface: the left is the inventory (up to 8 slots), the right is the chest (up to 10 slots), and the confirm key moves the selected item to the other side.

Chest methods

  • Overworld.ChestInteract(chest) opens the chest page.
    • chest the key name in the CHEST table; defaults to "chest" when omitted or passed "".
  • Chest.Show(chest) same as above, opens directly. chest is required — there is no default here; passing nil errors directly on #CHEST[chest].
  • Chest.Hide() closes.
  • Chest.Update() processes input, already wired by the engine.

Chest.Show() and ChestInteract() have different parameter rules

Only ChestInteract fills an empty chest name with "chest"; Chest.Show is bare and you must pass the correct name yourself.

The contents of a chest are defined in Game/Logics/init.lua, with the key name being the name passed above:

logic.chests = {
    chest  = {"Spider"},    -- the chest named chest contains one Spider
    chest1 = {},
}

It's full when it can't fit more (inventory 8 slots / chest 10 slots) — this is a hard cap.

docs.title: They All Lock the Player
docs.text:
All three interfaces set Char.controlling to false when opened and restore it when closed. So during the open period the player won't move and won't trigger any interaction.

But only the save page and chest page additionally call Overworld.JustOnDialog() once when closing (see Hide in save.lua / chest.lua):

Interface Locks player Calls JustOnDialog() on close Stat menu Yes No Save save page Yes Yes Chest chest page Yes Yes

JustOnDialog()'s role is to lock interactions on the closing frame, preventing "the confirm key used to close the interface" from conveniently triggering another onConfirm.

Copy these two lines when writing your own interface

Char.controlling = false
-- ... your interface ...
Char.controlling = true
Overworld.JustOnDialog()

JustOnDialog() is not optional: your interface is very likely also closed with the confirm key; without it, there's a high chance that closing the interface accidentally triggers the sign / warp point underfoot.

Frame-lock methods

  • Overworld.JustOnDialog() locks all interaction results for the current frame (only affects getInteractResult / onConfirm). Should be called once after closing any custom interface.

docs.title: Encounter
docs.text:
Overworld encounters are the "walk enough steps and bump into a monster" kind: the player accumulates a timer with each step, and when it fills, plays a ! animation then switches to the Battle scene.

Module path: Scripts/Libraries/Overworld/encounter.lua, exposed as the global Step.

docs.title: Starting an Encounter
docs.text:
Encounter methods

  • Overworld.InitEncounter(flag, start, range, amount) sets this map's encounter parameters.
    • flag the switch name used for the kill counter (stored in FLAG).
    • start base step count.
    • range an additional random 0 ~ range steps on top of start.
    • amount how many monsters this map can encounter in total.
  • Overworld.SetBattleScene(scene, game) specifies which Battle scene and which Encounter file to use after an encounter.
    • scene the scene name, e.g. "Battle.scene_battle_ow".
    • game the Encounter file name, e.g. "Poseur".
  • Overworld.Encounter(type) immediately triggers an encounter performance.
    • type the performance type; currently only "default" (omitted is also it).
ow.Init("Maps/main_scene/sol.lua")

-- encounter a monster every 100~160 steps, 12 monsters total on this map
ow.InitEncounter("test_killed", 100, 60, 12)
ow.SetBattleScene("Battle.scene_battle_ow", "Poseur")

More kills = slower encounters

The engine slows the pace based on how many FLAG[flag] has already killed:

rho = math.min(8, amount / (amount - killed))
time_target = rho * (start + math.random(range))

In other words, when only the last few are left, the interval is stretched up to 8× at most — exactly the original game's "monsters have been wiped out" behavior.

Four extra numbers appear in the terminal once running

Step.Init has a final line print(time_target, rho, start, range), left over from early debugging. Every InitEncounter prints this line of four numbers to the terminal — it's not an error, just ignore it.

docs.title: How Steps Are Counted
docs.text:
Step.UpdateTime() only increments when the player actually moved (pushing against a wall in place doesn't count). Already wired in char.Update by the engine — no need to call yourself.

The real "encounter when enough is accumulated" happens in Step.Update(), that line being called every frame by Overworld.Update.

Re-InitEncounter for every map

rho / time_target / _run are all file-level local variables in encounter.lua. When switching scenes, ow.Clear() calls ClearModuleTree("Scripts.Libraries.Overworld"), dropping and reloading the entire module — so time_target goes back to math.huge and _run goes back to true.

The result is not "carrying over the previous map's parameters", but that this run will never encounter anything (step.time >= time_target never holds), and no error is raised. So each map's InitEncounter / SetBattleScene must be written in that scene's own update or scene initialization.

Don't put InitEncounter in scene.update

Calling it every frame keeps resetting everything except step.time (and prints a line of numbers each frame). Putting it at the top level of the scene file, or guarding it with a flag on the first update, is enough.

docs.title: Nobody Came
docs.text:
When FLAG[flag] is already >= amount (monsters wiped out), walking another 60 steps triggers the original "Nobody came.":

  • The global variable OVERWORLD_NOBODYCAME is set to true.
  • Forces the Battle to switch to Battle.scene_battle_ow + the NobodyCame Encounter file.
  • After the performance ends, Overworld.ChangeScene resets it back to false.

To hook your own performance, just read this global variable to decide.

docs.title: Encounter Performance
docs.text:
After Overworld.Encounter(), there is a fixed-length interlude (counted in frames):

Frame What happens 0 ! pops above the player's head (uses spr_exc_f.png when lv >= 10) 60 ~ 90 ! disappears, black screen and Soul flash every 5 frames, with snd_tong.wav 90 Soul flies toward the Battle box position, with snd_encounter_fall.wav 130 Records current position and facing, switches to the Battle scene

docs.title: Bridging to the Battle Scene
docs.text:
It is recommended to use the engine's Scripts/Scenes/Battle/scene_battle_ow.lua, which does two extra things beyond a normal Battle scene:

  1. On entry, it pushes DATA.player's real data into Player (name, LV, max HP, current HP), and clears kr.
  2. On exit, it writes Battle.EXP / Battle.GOLD / remaining HP back into DATA, and settles the level-up according to DATA.lv_data (on level-up, max HP increases per the table, and the increase is added to current HP).

It also sets the ending scene to DATA.room, meaning after the fight you automatically return to the map you entered the Battle from.

Encounter-related globals

  • OVERWORLD_ENCOUNTER_BATTLE {Battle scene name, Encounter file name}, written by SetBattleScene.
  • OVERWORLD_NOBODYCAME whether in the "nobody came" state.
  • FLAG_KILLING_COUNTER the kill-counter switch name currently used for encounters, written by InitEncounter.
  • Battle.EXP / Battle.GOLD this Battle's earnings, cleared to zero after being written back.

To write your own bridge scene, copy scene_battle_ow.lua; the key is not to miss that write-back in scene.clear.

docs.title: Shop
docs.text:
The Shop is an independent scene, not a page overlaid on the Overworld. When the player walks to the shop door, switch scene into it; when leaving, switch back to DATA.room.

Main module: Scripts/Libraries/Overworld/shop.lua, obtained with ImportFile("Overworld.shop"). Scene: Scripts/Scenes/Overworld/Shops/scene_shop_0.lua, scene name Overworld.Shops.scene_shop_0.

docs.title: A Complete Shop Scene
docs.text:
local scene = {}
local shop = ImportFile("Overworld.shop")

-- what it says on entry, and what it says when choosing "Leave"
shop.SetMainText("* ​哇​咔​咔​咔​。\n* ​补牙​补牙​补牙​。")
shop.SetEndText("* ​下次​再来​哦​。")

-- shelf: fill in item ids, names looked up in ITEMS
shop.SetGoods({"CrabApple", "HotCat"})
shop.SetAmount("CrabApple", 4)              -- not set (or passed nil) = infinite stock
shop.SetBuyPrice("CrabApple", 7)
shop.SetBuyPrice("HotCat", 18)

-- right-side two columns: shopkeeper's quip + the intro panel that slides up
shop.SetBuyOpinion("CrabApple", "I\nmade\nthis.")
shop.SetIntroduction("CrabApple", "+20 HP")

-- no sell price = half the buy price (HotCat has no sell price set → 9G)
shop.SetSellPrice("CrabApple", 3)

-- rejection line: when an item with sell price 0 is selected, this plays instead of a deal
shop.SetCannotSellText("* ​我​这里​废品​已经​够​多​了​。")          -- whole-shop default
shop.SetCannotSellText("Stick", "* ​如果​我​的​店里​都​是​木棍​和​绷带​，\n  ​那​我​也​不用​开​商店​了​。")

-- talk topics: one per line in the list
shop.AddTalk("​天气​", {"* ​今天​也​一如既往​。", "* ​明天​大概​也​一样​。"})
shop.AddTalk("​时间​", "* ​地下​没有​白天​和​黑夜​。\n* ​所以​时间​只是​个​概念​。")
shop.SetQueue("​天气​", "​时间​")   -- bind into one queue, only one shown

-- background
local bg = shop.GetBackground()
bg:Scale(2, 2)
bg:SetAnimation({
    "Scene/Waterfall/spr_starpattern_0.png",
    "Scene/Waterfall/spr_starpattern_1.png",
}, 0.1)

function scene.update(dt)
    shop.Update(dt)
end

function scene.draw()
end

function scene.clear()
    shop.Clear()
    Layers.clear()
end

return scene

Both lines in scene.clear must be written, and the order cannot be reversed

shop.Clear() does two things: first it sets the _onComplete of the main text box and the opinion column to nil, then ClearModuleTree("Scripts.Libraries.Overworld.shop") unloads the module from the require cache.

The order exists for this reason: Layers.clear() internally calls Typers.ClearAll() first, destroying each typewriter via Destroy(), and Destroy() triggers _onComplete. If shop.Clear() weren't called first, on leaving the shop that callback would re-enter shop logic on a half-dead object.

The module must also be unloaded: on leaving, shop._leaving is set to true, and the first line of shop.Update is if (shop._leaving) then return end. If the module stays in the cache, entering the shop a second time will not respond to input at all.

docs.title: Interface and State Machine
docs.text:
The Shop has four actions, chosen by the player with the Soul:

Action Description Buy Open the shelf; confirm key deducts money at the SetBuyPrice price Sell Open your own inventory; confirm key adds money at the SetSellPrice price Talk Open the topic list; confirm key reads that topic Exit Leave, after saying SetEndText fade out back to DATA.room

Talk does not show SetMainText

SetMainText is the greeting shown in the bottom text box while idle (cursor on the four buttons). Talk opens the topic list, and the selected topic's body text borrows that same text box temporarily to display.

After choosing Buy / Sell / Talk, the list occupies the left column (5 rows per page, scrollable), with a red Soul as the cursor. For Buy / Sell, the right side simultaneously shows the shopkeeper's quip and the intro panel that slides up; for Talk, the right two columns clear.

The three actions block when there's nothing to show, play a line, then return to idle:

Case Trigger condition Line said (localization key) Shop buys nothing SetSellable(false) Overworld.Shop.Text.NoSelling Inventory is empty DATA.player.items is empty Overworld.Shop.Text.NoItems No topics Not a single AddTalk called Overworld.Shop.Text.NoTalk

docs.title: State Machine
docs.text:
IDLE → BUY / SELL / TALK, plus two transient states — they hand the whole screen (and the confirm key) to the main text box:

State Description Where it goes after IDLE Four buttons, cursor is a Soul — BUY / SELL / TALK List states Cancel key returns to IDLE MESSAGE A blocking line (not enough money, inventory full, topic body, rejection line) Returns to the state it entered from EXITING Farewell line on leaving After speaking, set _leaving, raise the black overlay and switch back to DATA.room

Why the frame lock exists

Typers.Update runs before scene.update, so "the confirm key that finished reading this line" is read again by shop.Update in the same frame. Without the lock, the confirm that closes the message would immediately re-open the list. The input_lock in the code exists for this.

docs.title: Key Bindings
docs.text: Key Idle In list confirm Enter selected action / leave Deal, read topic, read rejection line cancel — Return to idle up / down Move among the four buttons Move in the list (scrolls at the bottom)

docs.title: Method Reference
docs.text:
Text

  • shop.SetMainText(text) sets the line shown while idle. A string or a string array both work.
  • shop.GetMainText() reads it back (always an array, normalized internally).
  • shop.SetEndText(text) sets the line said on leaving.
  • shop.GetEndText() reads it back. Defaults to localization Overworld.Shop.Text.Leave.

Shelf and stock

  • shop.SetGoods(list) replaces the whole shelf.
    • list an array of item id strings, e.g. {"CrabApple", "HotCat"}.
    • An id not found in ITEMS is skipped, and [Shop] Unknown item id: xxx is printed.
    • Names are copied from ITEMS when added to the shelf; changing ITEMS afterwards does not affect items already on the shelf.
  • shop.AddGoods(id) adds one item to the end of the shelf.
  • shop.RemoveGoods(index) removes one by index.
  • shop.GetGoods() reads the shelf back (array of {id, name}).
  • shop.SetAmount(id, amount) sets stock.
    • amount passed nil = infinite stock (default); a number is clamped to >= 0.
  • shop.GetAmount(id) reads stock, returns math.huge when infinite.
  • shop.IsSoldOut(id) whether stock is <= 0.
    • Sold-out items stay on the shelf, but an extra Overworld.Shop.Text.SoldOut (​已​售罄​) is appended at the line end; selecting it and confirming only plays a sound, no money deducted.

Prices

  • shop.SetBuyPrice(id, price) sets the buy price.
  • shop.GetBuyPrice(id) reads the buy price, returns 0 if never set.
  • shop.SetSellPrice(id, price) sets the sell price.
  • shop.GetSellPrice(id) reads the sell price. When never set, returns half the buy price (rounded down), not 0:
shop.SetBuyPrice("CrabApple", 7)   -- SetSellPrice not called
print(shop.GetSellPrice("CrabApple"))   -- 3

Sell price 0 = the shop doesn't buy this item

Selecting an item with sell price 0 and confirming will not complete a deal, but plays a rejection line (see below). This is exactly the laziest way to write "don't buy this": set the sell price to 0 (or simply don't set a buy price either, in which case half of that is also 0). Note that for an item where SetBuyPrice was never even called, GetSellPrice also computes 0 — an item you forgot to set a buy price for cannot be sold.

Opinion and intro

  • shop.SetBuyOpinion(id, opinion) sets the quip shown on the right when buying.
  • shop.GetBuyOpinion(id) reads it back, defaults to localization Overworld.Shop.Opinion.Default (……) when unset.
  • shop.SetSellOpinion(id, opinion) sets the quip when selling.
  • shop.GetSellOpinion(id) reads it back, same default as above.
  • shop.GetOpinion(id) auto-selects by which list is currently open: the SELL page reads the sell one, the TALK page reads the topic-narration one, otherwise the buy one.
  • shop.SetIntroduction(id, text) sets the short description in the intro panel that slides up.
  • shop.SetIntroductions(map) batch: SetIntroductions({CrabApple = "+20 HP", HotCat = "+12 HP"}).
  • shop.GetIntroduction(id) reads it back, returns empty string "" when unset.

Don't format opinion text like dialogue

The right-column quip and intro panel are panel text, not dialogue. Starting with an asterisk-space, EText does a two-space hanging indent, which pushes the text right out of the right column. The topic body and rejection lines in the main text box still need the asterisk — those are real dialogue.

Sell toggle and rejection lines

  • shop.SetSellable(value) whether the shop buys anything, default true. After setting to false, choosing Sell only plays a line, no list opens.
  • shop.IsSellable() reads it back.
  • shop.SetNoSellText(text) the "shop buys nothing" line (used when SetSellable(false)).
  • shop.SetCannotSellText(id, text) sets the line for a single item being rejected. Passing a table as text means multiple segments, advancing one per confirm.
  • shop.SetCannotSellText(text) passing only one parameter = sets the whole-shop default rejection line.
  • shop.GetCannotSellText(id) the resolved result. Table in, table out: if you set multiple segments, you read back multiple segments.
  • shop.SetCannotSellTexts(map) batch: SetCannotSellTexts({Stick = "...", Bandage = {"...", "..."}}).
  • shop.GetCannotSellTexts() reads back that single-item table.
  • shop.ClearCannotSellTexts() clears all single-item lines (the whole-shop default stays).

The %s in a line is replaced with the item name:

shop.SetCannotSellText("Bandage", {"* ​我​可不​需要​%s。", "* ​拿走​拿走​。"})

Resolution order is single item → whole-shop default → localization Overworld.Shop.Text.CannotSell (* ​这个​我​不收​。).

A bare % in a line won't crash the shop

The copy is hand-written, and formatRefusal wraps string.format in a pcall. A broken format string is just displayed as-is, without dragging the whole shop down.

Money and misc

  • shop.GetGold() reads gold.
  • shop.SetGold(value) writes gold.
  • shop.SetMaxItems(count) inventory cap, default 8. Buying, selling, and that n/8 readout share this one value.
  • shop.GetMaxItems() reads it back.
  • shop.Refresh() redraws the gold/inventory readout; if a list is open, rebuilds the list too.
  • shop.GetPlayer() returns the red Soul sprite in the shop.
  • shop.GetBackground() returns the background sprite object; Scale / SetAnimation it yourself.
  • shop.Update(dt) called every frame, processes input and performance.
  • shop.Clear() see the danger note above.

Text box widths

  • shop.SetMainTextWidth(width) main text box width (greeting, rejection lines, topic body). Default 560 (panel x=40..600).
  • shop.SetOpinionWidth(width) right-column quip width. Default 170 (x=460..630).
  • shop.SetIntroWidth(width) intro panel width. Default 182 (x=448..630).
  • shop.SetTextWidths(main, opinion, intro) set all three at once; a nil argument leaves that item unchanged.
  • shop.SetAutoWrap(enabled) auto-wrap master switch, default on. When off, only hand-written \n is honored.
  • shop.IsAutoWrap() reads it back.

After changing widths, the engine conveniently re-lays out the three panels — EText reads size while typing, and InstText is pre-rendered, so it needs Rebuild().

docs.title: Talk Topics and Queues
docs.text:
A topic is always a browsable list — select and confirm to read. The body can be a single line, or an array (one segment per confirm):

shop.AddTalk("​天气​", "* ​今天​也​一如既往​。")
shop.AddTalk("​时间​", {"* ​地下​没有​白天​。", "* ​所以​时间​只是​个​概念​。"})

Topic methods

  • shop.AddTalk(topic, text) adds one, returns the new count.
    • Can also pass just a table: AddTalk({"​时间​", "* ​地下​没有​白天​。"}) or AddTalk({topic = "​时间​", texts = {...}}).
  • shop.SetTalks(list) replaces the whole thing. Pass either an array (each entry is one item) or a topic name = body map.
  • shop.RemoveTalk(index) deletes by index.
  • shop.ClearTalks() deletes all.
  • shop.GetTalks() reads back the original table (queues not collapsed, order is the AddTalk order).

docs.title: Queue: Squeeze several topics into one line
docs.text:
SetQueue binds several topics into one queue, showing only one of them at a time — whichever the dialogue has progressed to. After reading the current one, reveal the next; after all are read, wrap back to the first.

shop.SetQueue("​天气​", "​时间​")        -- only one of the two is shown
shop.SetQueue({"​天气​", "​时间​"})      -- same as above
shop.SetQueue(1, 2)                  -- can also pass AddTalk order numbers

Members are given by topic name or 1-based index, and are lazily resolved — SetQueue works whether written before or after AddTalk. Each call adds one queue, so a shop can have several independent queues; topics not in any queue always show.

Queue methods

  • shop.SetQueue(...) adds one queue, returns the new count.
  • shop.SetQueues(list) replaces the whole thing: SetQueues({{"​天气​", "​时间​"}, {"​出口​", "​秘密​"}}).
  • shop.ClearQueues() clears all.
  • shop.GetQueues() reads back the original table.
  • shop.GetVisibleTalks() reads the rows actually shown on the list right now, with queues already collapsed:
-- {{topic = "​天气​", texts = {...}, seen = 0, is_new = false}, ...}

docs.title: When does "(New)" actually appear
docs.text:
Here there are two easily-confused judgments, implemented as two different functions in the code:

Predicate Internal field Meaning Unread seen <= 0 determines which member the queue currently shows Flagged fresh == true determines whether "(New)" is appended at line end

The key point: "(New)" does not mean "unread", but "just revealed by the queue paging forward".

  • On entering the shop all topics are unfagged — even if you've never read them.
  • Only when the queue moves forward and reveals a not-yet-read member is that member flagged with "(New)".
  • Once read, the flag is cleared immediately. So after a queue completes one full cycle, there are no more "(New)".
  • Topics not in any queue never flag themselves — use SetTalkNew manually.

The flag appears as a localized "(New)" (Overworld.Shop.Text.New) appended at line end, with the whole row tinted new_color (default UNDERTALE yellow).

Progress and flag methods

  • shop.IsTalkNew(index) whether currently flagged "(New)".
  • shop.SetTalkNew(index, value) manually toggle "(New)". Use this when a topic is outside a queue.
  • shop.IsTalkUnread(index) never read?
  • shop.SetTalkSeen(index, seen) mark as read (true) / unread (false), and conveniently clears "(New)".
    • Setting to "unread" moves this member to the front of the queue — exactly the usage for restoring dialogue progress from a save.
  • shop.ResetTalkProgress() all topics back to unread, and each queue's pointer back to the first.
  • shop.SetNewColor(r, g, b) change the "(New)" color.

The index for all the above methods accepts either a topic name or a 1-based index.

docs.title: Right-column topic narration
docs.text:
When the topic list is open, the right column does not show the topic list, but the shopkeeper's quip about the topic under the current cursor.

It has a three-level resolution chain: single topic → whole-shop default → localization Overworld.Shop.TalkOpinion.Default.

shop.SetTalkOpinion("​想​聊点​什么​？")          -- only one parameter = whole-shop default
shop.SetTalkOpinion("​天气​", "​又​聊天​气​？")     -- two parameters = set a specific topic

Topic narration methods

  • shop.SetTalkOpinion(topic, opinion) with one parameter sets the whole-shop default; with two sets a specific topic's.
  • shop.GetTalkOpinion(topic) reads the resolved result. Passing topic as nil takes the whole-shop default layer.
  • shop.SetTalkOpinions(map) batch: SetTalkOpinions({​天气​ = "​又​聊天​气​？", ​时间​ = "……"}).
  • shop.GetTalkOpinions() reads back the single-topic table (excluding the whole-shop default).
  • shop.ClearTalkOpinions() clears all single-topic narrations, leaving the whole-shop default.

To make a topic return to default, you can't pass nil

SetTalkOpinion("​天气​", nil) is not treated as "clear the quip for ​天气​" — with one fewer parameter, it takes the one-parameter branch, setting the whole-shop default to the string "​天气​". To clear a single item, only ClearTalkOpinions() (clear all) works.
