docs.title: Audio System
docs.text:
Audio is the same: SE.audio is a direct forward of love.audio (see this topic's home page).

SE.audio.setVolume(0.5)                                     -- global volume
local src = SE.audio.newSource("Resources/Music/a.ogg", "stream")
src:play()

For daily audio playback, go through the engine's Audio library

Scripts/Libraries/Audio.lua is the engine's entry point for you, and it uses SE.audio at the bottom layer:

function audio.PlaySound(sound, volume, loop)
    local source = SE.audio.newSource(resolved_path, "static")
    source:setVolume(volume or Global.GetVariable("Volume").Master * ...)
    ...

Creating SE.audio.newSource yourself bypasses its Game-area override, path resolution, volume-follow, and lifecycle management; don't do it unless necessary.

docs.title: Which to use
docs.text:
What to do Use what Play a sound effect Audio.PlaySound(path, volume, loop) Play a music track Audio.PlayMusic(path, volume, loop) Whether a music is playing Audio.FindMusic(path) Pause / resume / stop an audio Audio.Pause(inst) / Audio.Resume(inst) / Audio.Stop(inst) Volume, pitch fade, fade in/out Controller ins:FadeIn / FadeOut / VolumeTransition / PitchTransition Loop segment (intro → loop → outro) ins:SetLoopingPoint / FollowLoop / FollowOutro Stop all audio at once Audio.Clear() Low-level operations none of the above cover SE.audio.*

Where audio files go, how the Game area overrides, what methods the controller has — see Audio. Below only covers the SE.audio layer.

docs.title: Creation
docs.text:
Function Effect newSource Build an audio source. Second argument is the load type: "static" reads the whole thing into memory (good for short SFX), "stream" reads while playing (good for music) newQueueableSource Build an audio source you can push data chunks into a queue yourself, for real-time synthesis or streaming playback

The engine's Audio library splits it this way: SFX use "static", music uses "stream".

docs.title: Global playback control
docs.text:
Function Effect play Play; can take multiple audio sources at once pause Pause stop Stop and return to the beginning setVolume Set the global volume multiplier, applied to all playing audio getVolume Read the global volume multiplier setMixWithSystem Whether to mix with other system sounds when playing

Don't use SE.audio.setVolume for game volume settings

It is the LÖVE-level global multiplier, which overrides the engine's volume system. The engine's volume is a global variable:

Global.GetVariable("Volume")   -- { Master = 1, Music = 1, Sounds = 1 }

The Audio library reads it every time it plays and auto-multiplies (SFX × Master * Sounds, music × Master * Music), so to change volume, change this variable (or use the in-game settings), don't touch SE.audio.

docs.title: 3D positioning
docs.text:
Function Effect setPosition / getPosition Listener position setOrientation / getOrientation Listener orientation setVelocity / getVelocity Listener velocity, for Doppler effect setDistanceModel / getDistanceModel Distance attenuation model setDopplerScale / getDopplerScale Doppler strength

This group is for 3D sound (along with Source:setPosition etc.), 2D pixel games generally don't need it; just know it exists.

docs.title: Effects
docs.text:
Function Effect setEffect Attach a scene effect (reverb, echo …) getEffect Get the currently attached effect getActiveEffects List of currently active effects getMaxSceneEffects Max scene effects attachable getMaxSourceEffects Max effects attachable to a single audio source isEffectsSupported Whether the current device supports effects

Check before use

Effects don't take effect on some platforms. When using them, first check if (SE.audio.isEffectsSupported()) then, don't attach directly.

docs.title: Recording and stats
docs.text: Function Effect getRecordingDevices Get the list of recording devices getActiveSourceCount Number of audio sources currently playing

docs.title: Common pitfalls
docs.text:
Omitting the load type in newSource, large files go entirely into memory

When the second argument is omitted, LÖVE guesses by file size; guess wrong and tens of MB of music gets read into memory at once (easily crashes on mobile). Get into the habit of explicitly writing "static" / "stream".

Audio sources you create yourself you must manage yourself

The engine's Audio library registers all audio sources it creates, uniformly doing fade updates and cleanup; the objects you SE.audio.newSource yourself are not on its list — you are responsible for when to stop and when to release them.

docs.text:
• This topic's home page — what the SE layer is, engine-built functions
  • Audio — the engine's Audio library, Game-area override, controller methods
  • Graphics Drawing — SE.graphics and all drawing functions

docs.title: Developer Tools
docs.text: The engine ships with some development-only debugging and assistive tools that let you inspect and modify the game's running state in real time, and visually generate assets — greatly improving debugging efficiency. The vast majority of these tools only take effect in development builds; they're automatically excluded when packaging for release and never enter the shipped game.

docs.title: Pages in This Topic
docs.text: Page Content Scene Assist Tools The engine's built-in tool scenes; the bezier easing editor (visually shape easing curves and export code) Object Debugger In-game click / drag sprites, change properties, four-point deformation, export object code Variable Debugger F8 variable tree + console, inspect and modify any field in the engine's memory in real time Engine Hotkeys Full table of F2 ~ F9 hotkeys: reload, fullscreen, hot-reload, debug info, hitboxes, the two debuggers Resource Preloading SE.Preload(...) / SE.PreloadAll() decode Game-area resources into cache ahead of time, avoiding first-reference stutter

docs.title: Tool Scenes
docs.text:
The engine ships some helper tool scenes for development, located in the Scripts/Scenes/TOOL/ and Scripts/Scenes/TEST/ directories. They are only used during development and are not part of the actual game flow; you can rewrite or even delete them at any time.

Like normal scenes, these are entered with Scenes.switchTo. To make one the startup scene, just change FirstRoom in conf_pure.lua:

Global.SetVariable("FirstRoom", "TOOL.TweenEase")

Scene path notation

The dot in Scenes.switchTo("TOOL.TweenEase") corresponds to the folder hierarchy: Scripts/Scenes/TOOL/TweenEase.lua → TOOL.TweenEase. The TEST directory works the same way, e.g. TEST.gb.

docs.title: Bezier Easing Editor
docs.text:
The easing library's Bézier curves can be hand-written with control points, or sculpted visually with this scene.

Open the scene TOOL.TweenEase, and you'll see operation buttons on the left and a coordinate-system canvas on the right: the horizontal axis is the time progress t (0~1), and the vertical axis is the eased output value (0~1). The more "bulged" the curve, the more pronounced the easing acceleration/deceleration.

docs.title: Meanings of the shapes on the canvas
docs.text:
Shape Meaning Green square Start/end anchors; the two ends of the curve must land on (0,0) and (1,1) Orange dot A middle control point that determines the curve's bend shape Yellow halo The currently selected point Blue curve The current Bézier easing curve Gray diagonal Linear reference line (y = x); the closer the curve hugs it, the closer to constant speed

The curve is evaluated using the De Casteljau algorithm, so the number of control points can be increased or decreased freely, not limited to cubic Bézier.

docs.title: Left-side buttons
docs.text: Button Action Add Point Add a new control point Delete Point Delete the currently selected control point Play Animation Play a preview animation once Export Animation Export the easing code

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
• Select / drag: Left-click a point inside the canvas to select it and start dragging; the point's coordinates are clamped to the [0,1] range. Click empty space to deselect.
  • Add a point: Add Point inserts a new point based on the current selection — when a middle point is selected, it inserts the midpoint between it and the next point; when nothing is selected, it inserts a point on the curve at t = 0.5.
  • Delete a point: Delete Point requires selecting a middle control point first; start/end anchors cannot be deleted. Attempting to delete them prints Cannot delete start or end anchor point to the terminal. The keyboard Delete / Backspace also triggers deletion.
  • Play preview: Play Animation moves a small red square along the curve from start to end; the canvas bottom shows t and y in real time, and a red vertical line marks the current progress.
  • Exit: Press Esc to quit the game.

docs.title: Exporting code
docs.text:
After clicking Export Animation, the code is printed to the terminal and written to Debug/exported_bezier.lua. The exported content registers a custom easing named myBezier via Tween.CreateCustomTween, in the form below:

--[[
  Exported Bezier Easing Curve
  Paste this code into your project, then use:
  tween.CreateTween(setter, "myBezier", "", beginVal, endVal, duration)
--]]

Tween.CreateCustomTween("myBezier", function(t)
    local pts = {
        {x = 0.0000, y = 0.0000},
        {x = 0.3300, y = 0.6700},
        {x = 0.6700, y = 0.3300},
        {x = 1.0000, y = 1.0000},
    }
    local n = #pts
    local px, py = {}, {}
    for i = 1, n do
        px[i], py[i] = pts[i].x, pts[i].y
    end
    for level = n, 2, -1 do
        for i = 1, level - 1 do
            px[i] = px[i] * (1 - t) + px[i + 1] * t
            py[i] = py[i] * (1 - t) + py[i + 1] * t
        end
    end
    return py[1]
end)

After pasting this into your project, you can use it just like a normal easing:

Tween.CreateTween(function(value)
    print(value)
    poseur.x = value
end, "myBezier", "", 0, 600, 60)

docs.title: A simpler approach
docs.text:
If you just want a fixed-shape Bézier easing, the library also provides Tween.CreateBezierEasing(name, points), which registers control points directly and is equivalent to the whole manual block above:

Tween.CreateBezierEasing("myBezier", {
    {x = 0,    y = 0},
    {x = 0.33, y = 0.67},
    {x = 0.67, y = 0.33},
    {x = 1,    y = 1},
})

Tween.CreateTween(function(value)
    print(value)
end, "myBezier", "", 0, 100, 60)

In other words: use the editor to sculpt the shape, then hand the exported control-point list to CreateBezierEasing — no need to keep that De Casteljau evaluation code around.

On easing names and direction

A custom easing's name itself does not distinguish type or direction; just pass the name directly as CreateTween's easingType and leave the direction parameter as an empty string "".

docs.title: Object Debugger
docs.text:
Debugger is an in-game object debugger that lets you click, drag, and edit properties of sprites directly on screen while the game is running, and export the tuned parameters as code. It's ideal for positioning, testing scale, experimenting with colors, and pulling four-point deformations — saving you from repeatedly editing code and restarting.

Library path: Scripts/Libraries/Engine/Debugger.lua

Development build only

This is a development tool, loaded only when _RELEASED is false (see conf.lua, imported by main.lua). It is not loaded in packaged release builds, so there's no leftover to worry about.

docs.title: Hotkeys
docs.text:
Key Action Ctrl + D Toggle debug mode (enter / exit interaction state) F9 Toggle the opacity of the on-screen info text (show / hide)

When exiting debug mode, the property panel, the right-click menu, and any four-point handle being dragged are all automatically collapsed.

Why it can block your view

The purpose of F9 is to let you hide that pile of object-property text covering the screen with one key, so you can see the result on a clean picture; open it again when needed.

docs.title: Selection and dragging
docs.text:
After entering debug mode:

  • Left-click an object to select it; the selected object gets a red border drawn around it.
  • Once selected, hold left-click and drag to move the object (there is a small drag threshold, so a slight click won't move it by accident).
  • Click empty space to deselect.

After selecting an object, all of its fields are printed item by item in the top-left of the screen, so you can inspect its values in real time.

docs.title: Right-click menu
docs.text:
After selecting an object, right-click opens a context menu. When the menu gets close to a screen edge it automatically flips / collapses to stay fully visible inside the screen.

Menu item Action Clone Create another object with the same path and layer Export Export the current object as code (see below) Delete Destroy the object flip X / flip Y Flip horizontally / vertically (negate the scale in that direction) Rotate 90° / Rotate -90° Rotate ±90 degrees Properties Show / hide the right-side property panel Toggle Four-Point Toggle four-point deformation mode Reset Corners Reset the four corners of the four-point deformation to the object's original rectangle

docs.title: Property panel
docs.text:
Opened via the Properties item in the right-click menu, located on the right side of the screen. You can edit directly these fields:

X, Y, ScaleX, ScaleY, Rot (rotation), Alpha (opacity).

Editing: click a field to start editing, type numbers, decimal points, and the minus sign directly, press Backspace to delete, Enter to apply, Esc to cancel.

If the object has a color field, a color swatch also appears at the bottom of the panel; click a swatch to change the object's color in real time, and the swatch for the current color gets a highlighted outline.

docs.title: Four-point deformation
docs.text:
When an object supports four-point deformation (has the _four_point field), you can enable it and drag the four corners to stretch and apply perspective freely.

Each handle has its own color for distinction:

Handle Position Color TL Top-left Red TR Top-right Green BL Bottom-left Blue BR Bottom-right Yellow
  • Click and drag a handle to move that corner.
  • When four-point deformation is on, dragging the object body moves all four corners together as one.
  • Reset Corners in the property panel restores the four corners to the object's original rectangle.

docs.title: Exporting objects
docs.text:
The Export item in the right-click menu writes the current object's full state as runnable code, output to Debug/exported_object.lua, and also printed to the terminal. The generated form is roughly:

-- Exported by Debugger
local spr = Sprites.CreateSprite("poseur.png", 0)
spr:MoveTo(320, 240)
spr:Scale(1, 1)
spr.rotation = 0
spr.alpha = 1
spr.color = {1, 1, 1}
spr.visible = true
spr:SetFourPointMode(true)
spr:SetFourPoint(
    260, 200,  -- top-left
    380, 200,  -- top-right
    260, 280,  -- bottom-left
    380, 280   -- bottom-right
)

Paste it into your scene code to reproduce the object you tuned.

docs.title: Making a sprite ignored
docs.text:
Some sprites are not meant to be selected or dragged by the debugger — for example a full-screen overlay, or a decorative background layer. Give them a flag:

spr.debugger_ignored = true

Once set, this sprite is completely skipped by the debugger — it cannot be selected, dragged, inspected, or exported.

docs.title: Variable Debugger
docs.text:
DevTool is the engine's runtime variable debugger. Pressing F8 pops up a separate tool window with two tabs:

  • Tree (variable tree): Expand the objects in the engine's memory level by level, and view and edit them directly.
  • Console: A sandboxed REPL where you can run expressions and assignment statements against the engine's global variables.

It differs in responsibility from the Object Debugger: the object debugger handles sprites on screen, while the variable debugger handles any table / field value.

Library path: Scripts/Libraries/Engine/DevTool.lua

Development build only

Like the object debugger, DevTool is loaded only when _RELEASED is false (see conf.lua, imported by main.lua, which calls Update / Draw). In the release build, F8 opens nothing.

Depends on SDL3

DevTool relies on Scripts/Libraries/Utils/Windows.lua to create a child window, which requires LÖVE 12 (ships with SDL3). If that library is unavailable, it prints [DevTool] Windows.lua / SDL3 not available. to the terminal and disables itself, without affecting the game itself.

docs.title: Opening and closing
docs.text:
Key Action F8 Open / close the tool window

The window stays closed until you first press F8. You can also call DevTool.Toggle() directly in code for the same effect.

The top-right of the title bar shows a KF:YES / KF:NO indicator, meaning whether this child window currently has system keyboard focus (see "The keyboard-input pitfall" below).

docs.title: Tab: Variable tree
docs.text:
You land on the Tree tab by default. At the top is a quick-edit bar, below it the variable-tree list. The top level of the tree is fixed to these root nodes:

Root node Content Player The Player object Battle The Battle system Overworld The Overworld system Scenes.current The current Scene Global (config) Global configuration _G (all globals) All global variables

These are live-read references; after a scene switch or when an object is replaced, they automatically re-point, with no manual refresh needed.

docs.title: Operations on the tree
docs.text:
• Expand / collapse: Click a table node's arrow or the node itself. A table node shows its child count, like table(12).
  • Edit number / string: Click such a leaf node to enter inline edit; press Enter when done to write back to real memory.
  • Toggle boolean: Click a boolean leaf node to negate it directly.
  • Rebuild children: Select a table node and press R to drop the cache and re-scan its children, used to refresh dynamically added/removed containers.

Cyclic references and functions

The tree automatically skips function fields and detects cyclic references (self-reference or mutual reference), avoiding infinite recursive expansion.

docs.title: Quick-edit bar
docs.text:
The two top inputs path / value read and write directly by path, handy for quickly changing a deeply nested field:

  • Fill a path in path, e.g. Player.hp, and press Enter to read the current value into the value box.
  • Fill a new value in value, and press Enter to write it back.
  • Press Tab to switch between the two inputs, Esc to exit input.

Paths support dots and brackets, e.g. Player.hp, Battle.enemies[1].hp.

docs.title: Tab: Console
docs.text:
The Console tab is a sandboxed REPL; type a line and press Enter to execute:

  • It first tries to evaluate as an expression; on success it prints the return value with an = prefix, e.g. typing 1 + 2 echoes = 3.
  • If the expression doesn't hold, it is then executed as a statement, e.g. Player.hp = 999.

Available global variables: Player, Battle, Overworld, Scenes, Global, _G.

The sandbox is mounted read-only and won't pollute globals

The console reads the engine globals via __index = _G; statements write to those tables in the engine itself (so Player.hp = 999 really does change the Player), but the sandbox environment itself won't stuff new global variables into _G.

Calling print(...) inside this sandbox is also redirected to the console rather than the terminal, handy for inserting debug output.

Scroll the wheel to review past output; press Esc to clear the current input.

docs.title: Hotkey quick reference
docs.text: Location Key Action Global F8 Open / close the tool window Tabs Click the title bar, or press T / C Switch to Tree / Console Quick-edit bar Enter Read value in path box, write value in value box Quick-edit bar Tab Switch between path / value boxes Quick-edit bar Esc Exit input Tree R Rebuild the selected node's children Tree Click number / string Inline edit, Enter applies Tree Click boolean Negate directly Console Enter Execute Console Esc Clear input

docs.title: The keyboard-input pitfall
docs.text:
This tool window is implemented with an SDL child window, but in the current LÖVE build, SDL child-window keyboard events are unreliable (you don't get key presses even when the window has focus). So the engine does this instead:

  • Key presses in the main window's love.keypressed are forwarded to DevTool.HandleKey, which handles character input and hotkeys uniformly;
  • Forwarding happens only when the tool window has focus, or the mouse is hovering over the tool window (decided by DevTool.WantsKeys());
  • While forwarding, the game scene still receives these keys as usual, so using the tool and playing the game don't steal input from each other.

When you click into the tool window, it tries to request keyboard focus from the system — that's where the title-bar KF:YES / KF:NO indicator comes from. If focus can never be obtained, just move the mouse over the tool window and input works normally too.

docs.title: Engine Hotkeys
docs.text:
The engine has a set of operation and debugging hotkeys. Most take effect only in the development build (_RELEASED = false) and are automatically disabled after packaging.

Hotkey Action Scope F2 Reload localization text, re-run both conf_pure configs, and switch to F2Room All versions F4 Toggle fullscreen / window All versions F5 Hot reload: clear cached engine modules and Game-area content, re-enter the current scene, and re-apply Hacks Dev build only F6 Print a debug info dump to the console (FPS, resolution, scale, current scene, input devices, sprite count, layer count, Hack report) Dev build only F7 Toggle Battle collision boxes (Battle.ToggleHitboxes(), inside the Battle scene) Dev build only F8 Toggle the variable debugger (DevTool) Dev build only F9 Toggle the object debugger (Debugger) info-text show/hide Dev build only

About F3

The engine has no F3, nor an FPS overlay. To see the frame rate, use the FPS field printed by F6, or press F8 to open the variable debugger and read the live value.

docs.title: F2 — Reload config and localization
docs.text: Re-read the language file, re-execute both engine and Game conf_pure.lua, then jump to the scene specified by F2Room. Use it when you've changed copy or config and want to see the effect immediately.

docs.title: F4 — Fullscreen toggle
docs.text: Switch between window and fullscreen, while recomputing the canvas scale; the border scales along with it.

docs.title: F5 — Hot reload
docs.text: More thorough than F2: clears the Scripts.Libraries and Game-area module caches, re-enters the current scene, then reloads Game/Hacks/. No need to restart the game after changing code.

docs.title: F6 — Debug info
docs.text: Prints a set of current state to the console: frame rate, window resolution, canvas scale, current scene name, virtual-keyboard and gamepad counts, sprite count, layer-object count, and the Hack registration status. Good for quickly confirming the environment.

docs.title: F7 — Battle collision boxes
docs.text: Only meaningful inside the Battle scene, used to visualize perfect-pixel hitboxes. Related content: Collision and Battle Scene and Callbacks.

docs.title: F8 / F9 — The two debuggers
docs.text: F8 opens the variable debugger, and F9 controls the object debugger info-text show/hide. See their respective pages for the division of labor.

docs.title: Custom hotkeys
docs.text:
The hotkeys are written in main.lua's love.keypressed:

  • Global hotkeys (F2 / F4 / F5 / F6 / F8) check key directly.
  • F7 inside Battle is polled every frame by Battle via Keyboard.GetState("f7").

To add your own hotkey, copy the corresponding block and change the key name.

docs.title: ❕️ Asset Preloading
docs.text:
Decode an entire directory of assets into the cache in advance, so that the first use of Sprites.CreateSprite and Audio.PlaySound / PlayMusic afterwards no longer stutters.

Once the resources under Game/Resources/ grow, entering a scene often "hitches" for a moment — because each image and each piece of audio is decoded only the first time it is referenced. SE.Preload lets you decode them all at the right moment (e.g. during a scene transition, or in a loading screen), so subsequent calls hit the cache directly.

Preloading only walks the Game area (Game/Resources/), and won't touch the main Resources/. The main resource directory often has thousands of files; running through it all could freeze for tens of seconds, so the engine deliberately leaves it alone.

docs.title: SE.Preload
docs.text:
SE.Preload("Sprites/Test")          -- All images under Game/Resources/Sprites/Test/
SE.Preload("Music", "Sounds/ui")    -- Preload multiple directories at once
SE.Preload("Sprites/")              -- Trailing slash optional

The parameter is a variable number of path strings; each path is normalized to a Game-area directory and then traversed recursively (including all subfolders).

Path syntax Directory actually traversed "Music" The whole Game/Resources/Music/ tree "Sprites/Test" The whole Game/Resources/Sprites/Test/ tree "Sounds/ui/voice" The whole Game/Resources/Sounds/ui/voice/ tree (multi-level sub-paths also work) "Game/Resources/Music" Equivalent to "Music"

The return value is the actual number of files handed to the loader, which you can use to show progress in a loading screen.

docs.title: Type names in the path
docs.text:
The first segment of the path must be a resource type the engine knows:

Type name Loaded into Corresponding basics page Sprites Sprite cache (sprites.cache) Sprites Sounds Sound cache (Audio.cache, static) Audio Music Music cache (Audio.cache, stream) Audio Fonts Font cache Fonts

A non-matching type name prints a WARNING and skips that path, without crashing.

docs.title: Extension dispatch
docs.text:
The loader is chosen by file extension, and when it disagrees with the folder type, the extension wins (a .wav placed under Sprites/ is still treated as audio):

  • Images: png / jpg / jpeg / bmp / tga / hdr / dds
  • Audio: wav / ogg / mp3 / flac / aiff / it / xm / mod / s3m
  • Fonts: ttf / ttc / otf / fnt

Other suffixes (README.md, .txt, etc.) are silently skipped.

docs.title: SE.PreloadAll
docs.text:
SE.PreloadAll()

Run through the entire Game/Resources/ once. Returns the number of files loaded.

Use PreloadAll with care

This traverses all resources in the Game area; if your Game area also has hundreds of files, calling it once before entering the game still causes noticeable stutter. The recommended approach is to SE.Preload just those sub-directories per scene, on demand.

docs.title: When to call
docs.text:
Preloading itself is a one-time synchronous operation (traverse + decode), best placed at moments with no rendering pressure:

  • A loading screen (if you have a custom loading scene).
  • Inside a scene's init callback, before creating the first batch of sprites / playing the first batch of audio.
  • A transition frame before switching scenes.

Don't call it every frame, and don't stuff it into update — the whole point of preloading is "once ahead of time"; repeated calls only refresh the timestamp and won't redo the decode, but they still traverse the directory for nothing.

docs.title: Relationship with CreateSprite / PlaySound
docs.text:
After preloading, the caller is completely unaware:

  • Sprites.CreateSprite("foo.png") still looks up sprites.cache by path as usual — hits it and uses it directly, otherwise decodes; preloading just makes the "hit" happen earlier.
  • Audio.PlaySound("foo.wav") / PlayMusic clones a template Source from Audio.cache to use; the clone shares the underlying decoded buffer (sound) or file handle (music), so it doesn't re-decode on every play.

In other words: after calling SE.Preload, write your game logic's CreateSprite / PlaySound exactly as before — cache reuse is automatic.

docs.title: Design notes
docs.text:
• Game area only: The main Resources/ is deliberately left alone. Put the resources you want to preload under Game/Resources/Sprites/<subdir>/ and the like, then use SE.Preload("Sprites/<subdir>") to precisely warm them up.
  • Idempotent: Re-preloading the same path won't re-decode, only refreshes the cache timestamp. So repeatedly entering/leaving a scene is safe.
  • Doesn't create instances: Sprites.PreloadFile only stuffs the image and ImageData into the cache, it doesn't actually draw to the screen. Whether to display it, and where, is still decided by your later CreateSprite.
  • LRU still applies: Images loaded by preloading are still subject to LRU reclamation via OPT_LRU_SPRITES; those not referenced by any sprite for a long time get cleared — following the same lifecycle as normally loaded images.

docs.title: Localization
docs.text:
Localization (L10n) pulls all player-facing text out of the code and into JSON files. In the code you only write "keys"; at runtime a Lua library looks up the table, replaces placeholders, and produces the actual text for the current language.

Three pieces:

Role Path Description Engine default translations Localization/ The engine's own copy (en.json, zh_CN.json), fallback Game override translations Game/Localization/ Your game's copy goes here, same-named files are layered on top of the engine's Lookup & replace library Scripts/Libraries/Localize.lua Reads files, looks up keys, does string.format replacement

'Game first' is an engine-wide convention

It's not just translations — sprites, sounds, waves, maps, etc. all follow the "first Game/, then the engine directory" order. The full mapping is in Basic Development → Game Area & Resource Override.

docs.title: The Flow in One Line
docs.text:
Global.SetVariable("Language", "zh_CN") in Game/conf_pure.lua
        ↓
main.lua calls Localize.setFile(Global.GetVariable("Language")) at startup
        ↓
Localize reads the two layers Game/Localization/zh_CN.json and Localization/zh_CN.json,
        Game-layer keys override engine-layer keys, Game-unwritten keys fall back automatically
        ↓
dkjson decodes and merges into one flat "key → text" table
        ↓
In code: Localize.localizeText("Battle.Spare", {...})
        ↓
Look up table + string.format replace %s → return final string (or array)

docs.title: Pages in This Topic
docs.text: Page Content Directories & Language Files Priority of the two directories, how to choose a language, how to add a new language, hot reload Lookup & Replacement All uses of localizeText, dynamic keys, consequences of missing keys, typewriter tags

docs.title: Minimal Example
docs.text:
Add a key to Game/Localization/zh_CN.json:

{
  "MyGame.Greeting": "* Hello, %s!"
}

Fetch it in code:

local text = Localize.localizeText("MyGame.Greeting", {Player.name})
-- -> "* Hello, Frisk!"

After editing, press F2 to reload translations — no game restart needed.

docs.title: Directories and Language Files
docs.text:
Localization recognizes only two directories, and the files are one JSON per language.

Directory Belongs to Priority Game/Localization/ Your game ① Checked first Localization/ Engine default ② Fallback

Files in the directories are named <language code>.json, e.g. en.json, zh_CN.json. The current state of both directories in the project:

Localization/
├── en.json          ← Engine-bundled English
└── zh_CN.json       ← Engine-bundled Chinese

Game/Localization/
└── README.md        ← Currently empty; you need to put JSON in it yourself

docs.title: Lookup order
docs.text:
The two same-named files are not an either/or, but layered: Game/Localization/ is the high-priority patch layer, and the engine's copy is the fallback layer.

The candidate layers in the source (Scripts/Libraries/Localize.lua top) are ordered from high to low priority:

local ROOT_LOCALIZATION = "Localization/"          -- ② Fallback
local GAME_LOCALIZATION = "Game/Localization/"     -- ① Patch
local LAYER_PATHS = { GAME_LOCALIZATION, ROOT_LOCALIZATION }

At load time, every existing layer is read and merged (mergeInto) starting from the lowest priority, with the higher priority overwriting key by key:

Case Result Game area has "A", engine doesn't Use Game area's A Both sides have "A" Game area wins Game area didn't write "A" Automatically falls back to the engine's copy

The Game area only needs to write the entries you want to change

For example, put only one line in Game/Localization/zh_CN.json:

{
  "Battle.EnemiesName.Sol": "Sol"
}

The rest of the hundreds of keys (Battle buttons, menu, save page…) are still taken from Localization/zh_CN.json, and the terminal won't spit [L10N WARNING] Missing localization key.

Arrays are replaced wholesale, not merged by index

Array values like "Battle.GameoverText": ["* A", "* B"] are fully replaced once the Game area writes them. If you only want to change one segment, you still have to copy the whole array over and edit it.

A corrupted JSON in some layer is skipped

When the Game-area copy fails to parse, it only prints ... (layer skipped) and keeps using the engine's copy; it won't take down the whole language, nor won't fall back to en. (It only falls back to en if both layers are broken.)

docs.title: How to confirm which copy is currently in use
docs.text:
At startup the terminal prints all layers that participated in the merge, with the higher priority on the left of the arrow:

[L10N] L10n has started successfully, using language: zh_CN (Game/Localization/zh_CN.json > Localization/zh_CN.json)

You can also query anytime:

print(Localize.GetLanguagePath("zh_CN"))   -- the highest-priority path
print(Localize.currentFile)                -- same as above, the main source of the loaded language
print(table.concat(Localize.GetSources(), " > "))   -- all layers participating in the merge, by priority

docs.title: Choosing a language
docs.text:
The language is set in the two conf_pure.lua files, and the Game-area copy runs later and overrides the engine's:

-- conf_pure.lua (engine root)
Global.SetVariable("Language", "en")
Global.SetVariable("Language", "zh_CN")    -- Writing the same variable twice: the later one wins

If your game wants to specify it, change the same line in Game/conf_pure.lua (that whole file is just the root's copy pasted then changed).

At startup main.lua reads it:

Localize.setFile(Global.GetVariable("Language"))

Language must be a string

The first line of setFile is if (type(language) ~= "string") — passing nil prints [L10N WARNING] Invalid language file. and then returns directly, loading no language at all. The next first call to localizeText will lazily load en, but currentLanguage is still nil, and places depending on it (like the virtual keyboard deciding Chinese vs English) will treat it as English.

docs.title: No restriction on language codes
docs.text:
en, zh_CN, zh_TW, ja, ko … name them freely, as long as they match the filename. The only thing that parses it is the virtual keyboard, which judges Chinese by the first two characters:

if (code and code:sub(1, 2):lower() == "zh") then return "zh" end

docs.title: Adding a new language
docs.text:
Take adding Japanese as an example:

  1. Copy Localization/en.json to Game/Localization/ja.json (put it in the Game area to avoid editing the engine directory; the Game area now automatically overlays on top of the engine's copy, so writing only your words also works, but for a full translation it's still recommended to copy completely first then change)
  2. Translate entry by entry, only change the value to the right of the colon, don't touch a single character of the key on the left
  3. In Game/conf_pure.lua, change to Global.SetVariable("Language", "ja")
  4. Run the game and check whether the terminal prints using language: ja (Game/Localization/ja.json)
  5. After that, edit the JSON and press F2 to hot-reload

Missing keys are no longer fatal, but still print a warning

If you miss an entry while translating, or mistype a key name, at runtime it's just one line [L10N WARNING] Missing localization key: ..., it won't crash, but the player will see blank or garbled text. Because the Game area automatically falls back to the engine's copy, a missing key only affects the part you newly wrote.

docs.title: Hot reload
docs.text:
Key Behavior F2 Localize.reload() + re-execute both conf_pure.lua + switch to the F2Room scene F5 In dev mode, additionally clears the module cache and re-runs Hacks (including Localize.reload()) 
function localize.reload()
    if localize.currentLanguage then
        localize.setFile(localize.currentLanguage)
    else
        print("[L10N WARNING] No language loaded to reload.")
    end
end

To change language, change conf then F2

reload() only re-reads the file for the current language. To switch to another language, you must first change Language in conf_pure.lua, then press F2 (F2 re-runs conf). Pressing F2 directly won't switch languages.

When switching languages at runtime, remember to clear the cache

The virtual keyboard caches its label lookups; after changing language call once:

VirtualKeyboard.ClearLabelCache()

docs.title: Structure of the JSON file
docs.text:
The engine's translation table is flat: the key is a whole dot-separated string.

{
  "Battle.Spare": "Spare",
  "Battle.HP.NotFull": "* You recovered %s HP!",
  "Overworld.Menu.Buttons": ["Item", "Stat", "Phone"]
}
Value type Allowed Note String ✅ Most common, may contain placeholders like %s Array ✅ Multi-segment text (e.g. GameoverText), or pure numeric values (e.g. menu coordinates) Number / Boolean ❌ Prints Invalid localization value and returns nil Nested object ⚠️ Can be stored in but cannot be retrieved (key lookup is flat file["xxx"])

Nested objects cannot be retrieved

The lookup implementation is local file = ...; current = file[key] — one step, nohierarchical descent. A nested structure like "Items": {} can be written in but not read out (nor is it used anywhere in the engine).

"Items": { "Candy": { "name": "Candy" } }   // ✗ Cannot be retrieved
"Items.Candy.name": "Candy"                  // ✓ This is the way

BOM is actually let through by dkjson, but still don't include it

dkjson's scanwhite skips a leading UTF-8 BOM, so a translation file with BOM usually still reads. But the engine's SafeJson explicitly rejects a BOM (see Advanced Development → JSON library). For convenience, always save as UTF-8 (without BOM).

Path is case-sensitive

The engine reads the disk directly with love.filesystem.read("Localization/zh_CN.json"). On Windows case doesn't matter, but once packaged to Android / Linux the whole thing won't be read. Filenames must be all-lowercase language code + .json.

What's read is love.filesystem's search path

That is, "save directory first, then game directory". If you used love.filesystem.write to write a same-named file into the save directory, it will override the in-game copy.

docs.title: Appendix: what if you want "full override"
docs.text:
Key-based merging is now the default behavior. If you genuinely want a language to be completely unaffected by the engine's copy (e.g. a new-version story rewrote all battle copy and you don't want to inherit any old values), don't count on deleting the engine file — just write out all the keys that language needs in the Game area; missing keys will still fall back to the engine's copy.

To truly disconnect, you can only give that language a value in the Game area that doesn't contain the key, or give the language a name for which the engine directory has no corresponding file (in which case only the Game layer exists).

docs.title: Lookup and Substitution
docs.text:
There is only one entry point for lookup:

Localize.localizeText(key)
Localize.localizeText(key, substitution parameters)

Localize is global (imported at main.lua startup via ImportFile("Localize")), so it can be called directly anywhere.

docs.title: Two ways to write the key
docs.text:
Style Example Note String "Battle.Spare" Most common Table {"Battle", "Spare"} Joined internally with ., equivalent to the above 
Localize.localizeText("Battle.Spare")
Localize.localizeText({"Battle", "Spare"})     -- the same key

Only string elements in the table get joined

When joining, it's if type(elements[i]) == "string" that is collected; numbers and booleans are silently dropped. If the result is an empty table it returns nil and prints Invalid localization key table..

docs.title: Substitution parameters (formats)
docs.text:
The second parameter is handed to string.format, supporting all placeholders like %s %d %f %x.

"Battle.HP.NotFull": "* You recovered %s HP!"

Localize.localizeText("Battle.HP.NotFull", {12})
-- -> "* You recovered 12 HP!"

docs.title: Multiple placeholders
docs.text:
Fill them in order; the wrong order makes the text come out wrong:

"Battle.WinTexts1": "* You won![wait:0.5]\n* You got %s XP and %s gold.\n"

Localize.localizeText("Battle.WinTexts1", {exp, gold})

docs.title: A single value doesn't need a table wrapper
docs.text:
If what you pass isn't a table, the engine wraps it itself:

Localize.localizeText("Battle.HP.NotFull", 12)      -- equivalent to {12}

Mismatched parameters return the original text

When string.format fails (not enough parameters, wrong type, extra %), the engine does not error, it only prints a line [L10N WARNING] string.format failed for key: ..., then returns the string with %s verbatim. The player will see the literal %s.

Localize.localizeText("Battle.HP.NotFull")       -- forgot to pass parameters
-- -> "* You recovered %s HP!"   ← comes out verbatim, placeholder not substituted

docs.title: Return value is not just a string
docs.text:
The looked-up value has two legal types, with different return behavior:

Value in JSON Without formats With formats String Return string after substitution Same as left Array Return the whole array as-is Per-element substitution on each string element, return a new array 
"Overworld.Menu.Buttons": ["Item", "Stat", "Phone"],
"Battle.GameoverText": ["* Our fate\n  rests on you...", "* %s![wait:0.5]\n  Hold your determination..."],
"Overworld.Menu.Interval": [215, 312, 425]

Localize.localizeText("Overworld.Menu.Buttons")[1]           -- "Item"
Localize.localizeText("Battle.GameoverText", {Player.name})  -- array, both lines had %s substituted
local x = tonumber(Localize.localizeText("Overworld.Menu.Interval")[1])  -- 215

The localization file is also used to store layout values

Overworld.Menu.Interval is a set of x coordinates, not text. Because buttons differ in length across languages, putting coordinates into the translation file is a reasonable usage.

Non-string elements in an array are kept as-is

During per-element substitution else result[i] = current[i] — numbers are not processed by string.format.

docs.title: Dynamically joined keys
docs.text:
Keys can be assembled at runtime; this is for "configuring different text per enemy / per action". The engine's Battle scene does exactly this:

-- Scripts/Scenes/Battle/scene_battle_init.lua:24
Battle.BattleDialogue(
    Localize.localizeText("Battle.Actions.Texts." .. enemy.id .. "." .. action.id),
    "ACTIONSELECT"
)

The corresponding keys in JSON:

"Battle.Actions.Texts.Poseur.Check": ["* Poseur[wait:0.5] - 0 ATK 0 DEF..."],
"Battle.Actions.Texts.Poseur.Pose":  ["* You and Poseur strike a pose..."]

A joined key won't auto-find its parent

If Battle.Actions.Texts.Poseur.Pose doesn't exist, it just doesn't exist; it won't fall back to Battle.Actions.Texts.Poseur. Miss one enemy and you miss a stretch of dialogue.

docs.title: Where the engine looks up keys
docs.text:
Location Keys used Game/Encounter/*.lua Battle.Narration.Default, Battle.EnemiesName.*, Battle.Actions.Names.* Scripts/Scenes/Battle/scene_battle*.lua Battle.Actions.Texts.<enemy>.<action> Scripts/Scenes/scene_gameover.lua Battle.GameoverText Scripts/Libraries/Overworld/stat.lua Overworld.Menu.Buttons / .Item / .Stat / .Interval Scripts/Libraries/Overworld/shop.lua Overworld.Shop.Action.<action> Scripts/Libraries/Overworld/Pages/save.lua Overworld.Save.Buttons / .Success Scripts/Libraries/Overworld/Pages/chest.lua Overworld.Chest.Title / .Tip Scripts/Waves/nobody_came.lua Overworld.Text.NobodyCame Scripts/Libraries/Controller/VirtualKeyboard.lua VirtualKeyboard.*

For the full list of engine-bundled keys, see Localization/zh_CN.json directly, grouped by prefix:

Prefix Manages what Battle.Narration.* The first narration line when entering Battle Battle.Spare / .Flee Battle buttons Battle.HP.* Heal prompt Battle.Items.Page / Battle.WinTexts* Item pagination, victory settlement Battle.GameoverText The two game-over lines Battle.EnemiesName.<enemy id> Enemy name Battle.Actions.Names.<action id> Action name in the ACT menu Battle.Actions.Texts.<enemy id>.<action id> The lines spoken after selecting an action Overworld.Menu.* Menu buttons, STAT panel layout Overworld.Save.* / Overworld.Chest.* Save page, chest page Overworld.Shop.Action.* Shop buy/sell/talk/leave VirtualKeyboard.* Virtual keyboard editor UI text

Adding translation for your own enemy

  1. Write Localize.localizeText("Battle.EnemiesName.Sol") in Game/Encounter/<your enemy>.lua
  2. Add "Battle.EnemiesName.Sol": "Sol" in Game/Localization/<language>.json
  3. Press F2 to reload

The key name can be anything, as long as both sides match; but following the engine's prefixes is easier to maintain.

docs.title: What happens when a key is missing
docs.text:
if current == nil then
    print("[L10N WARNING] Missing localization key: " .. tostring(elements))
    return nil
end

It doesn't error, it returns nil. But this nil is handed directly to the caller:

-- In battle: nil goes straight into the typewriter
Battle.BattleDialogue(Localize.localizeText("..."), "ACTIONSELECT")

Typers.EText.New(nil, ...) will blow up later when iterating the text — the symptom is "crashes only after you press", rather than quietly showing blank. So when you see Missing localization key in the terminal, don't treat it as noise; it's a signal of impending crash or display glitch.

Looking up keys every frame spams warnings

Menu-type code redraws every frame and looks up keys every frame; miss one key and that's 60 lines of warnings per second. Either fill in the key, or cache the result yourself like the virtual keyboard does.

docs.title: Typewriter tags pass through verbatim
docs.text:
The [wait:0.5], [speed:0.05], in translation text are not handled by the localization layer; localizeText only does string.format, and the tags are handed to the typewriter verbatim for interpretation.

"Battle.Narration.Default": "* Poseur struck[wait:0.5]
  [speed:0.05]a pose!"

When writing JSON, line breaks are

JSON can't have a direct line break; you must write the escape. The typewriter's layout (like two-space indentation) is achieved with spaces in the string, so preserve those spaces when translating.

docs.title: Virtual keyboard's special channel
docs.text:
The virtual keyboard doesn't call localizeText directly, but goes through its own VirtualKeyboard.L(key):

function VirtualKeyboard.L(key)
    -- ① First look up "VirtualKeyboard." .. key
    local full = VirtualKeyboard.l10nPrefix .. key
    local ok, value = pcall(l.localizeText, full)
    cached = (ok and type(value) == "string" and value ~= "") and value or false
    if (cached) then return cached end

    -- ② If not found, use the built-in word set
    local set = LABEL_SETS[resolveLanguage()] or LABEL_SETS.en
    return set[key] or LABEL_SETS.en[key] or key
end
Field / function Action VirtualKeyboard.useLocalize Default true; turn off to use only the built-in word set VirtualKeyboard.l10nPrefix Default "VirtualKeyboard." VirtualKeyboard.SetLanguage("zh"/"en"/table) Force-specify; passing a table means a custom whole word set VirtualKeyboard.ClearLabelCache() Clear cache, must call after switching language at runtime

It's the only module with a built-in fallback word set

Other modules get nil on a missing key; the virtual keyboard falls back to LABEL_SETS.en on a missing key, at most showing English, no crash. To change its text, add VirtualKeyboard.<key> to the JSON.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
Value being number/boolean returns nil

Only string and table are legal. Writing "Battle.Foo": 123 prints Invalid localization value for key: ... and returns nil.

Don't write trailing commas or comments in JSON

dkjson's tolerance for loose JSON is limited (it supports // and /* */ comments, but not trailing commas). A parse failure falls back to en and prints position info:

[L10N WARNING] Invalid language file.
               Using default language. (en)
[L10N Error]   ... JSON parse error at position 123 in ...: ...

Use that position to locate the character directly.

Changed translation but it didn't take effect? Check in this order

  1. Does the terminal line using language: xxx (path) point to the file you edited
  2. Did you forget to press F2 after editing
  3. Did the JSON fail to parse (there would be an Invalid language file warning)
  4. Is the key name misspelled (there would be a Missing localization key warning)
  5. Is the Chinese garbled (file encoding should be UTF-8)

docs.title: Networking
docs.text:
The networking topic covers the engine's three built-in networking/multiplayer libraries. They're independent of each other; use whichever you need:

Role Path What it does GameJolt API Scripts/Libraries/GamejoltAPI.lua Connect to GameJolt: login, achievements (trophies), scoreboards, cloud saves Discord RPC Scripts/Libraries/DiscordRPC.lua Show "what you're playing" on your Discord profile (Rich Presence) sock Scripts/Libraries/Network/sock.lua ENet-based multiplayer (C/S structure, event send/receive)

Two global aliases are set up at the top of main.lua — use them directly:

Gamejolt = ImportFile("GamejoltAPI")
Discord  = ImportFile("DiscordRPC")

sock is not auto-loaded (not every game needs multiplayer), so import it yourself when needed:

local sock = ImportFile("Network.sock")

docs.title: What the Engine Already Does for You
docs.text:
All three libraries are "quiet" by default and won't crash the game just because they're unconfigured.

Library What the engine does for you What you do Discord In love.load() reads Global.GetVariable("DiscordAppID") → Discord.init() → setActivity(); in love.update(dt) calls Discord.update(dt) every frame; in love.quit() calls Discord.shutdown() Change DiscordAppID in Game/conf_pure.lua to your own Gamejolt In love.update(dt) calls Gamejolt.update(dt) every frame (only drives the session heartbeat) You must call Gamejolt.init() and authUser() yourself — the engine won't do it for you sock None Write it all yourself

GameJolt does not auto-initialize

The engine only calls Gamejolt.update(dt) — nowhere does it call Gamejolt.init(). Calling other methods before init() will error directly because gamejolt.base_url is still nil (concatenating nil). See GameJolt.

docs.title: Dependencies & Platform Support
docs.text:
Library Dependency Consequence if unavailable Gamejolt Native https module (Resources/Libs/https.dll, Windows only) All requests return false, "GameJolt API unavailable on ...", game runs normally Discord LuaJIT's ffi + native libs under Resources/Libs/DiscordRPC/ (Windows only) init() returns false, reason, other methods degrade to no-ops sock enet (bundled with LÖVE, no extra dll needed) + optional bitser require "enet" failing will error directly (all standard LÖVE builds include it)

Android / Mobile

Both https.dll and discord-rpc-*.dll are Windows-only dynamic libraries and can't be loaded even if packed into an Android package. These two libraries auto-degrade on non-Windows platforms (isAvailable() returns false) — don't hang critical logic on them.

docs.title: Pages in This Topic
docs.text: Page Content GameJolt Initialization, login, achievements, session heartbeat, cloud saves, scoreboards, plus the unencoded-URL pitfall Discord RPC Changing Presence, callback events, image assets, byte limit, the origin of jit.off sock Multiplayer Server/client, events & schema, send modes & channels, a complete minimal example

docs.title: Minimal Examples
docs.text:
Discord — just change the config

-- Game/conf_pure.lua
Global.SetVariable("DiscordAppID", "1234567890123456789")  -- note: it's a string

About 2 seconds after entering the game, the activity status appears on your Discord profile.

GameJolt — you must initialize it yourself

-- in some scene's load
Gamejolt.init(Global.GetVariable("GamejoltID"), Global.GetVariable("GamejoltPK"))
local ok, err = Gamejolt.authUser("my_name", "my_token")
if (ok) then
    Gamejolt.sessionUpdate(30, "active")   -- the engine pings for you every frame after this
end

sock — both ends must run

-- server
server = sock.newServer("*", 22122)
server:on("chat", function(data, client) server:sendToAll("chat", data) end)
-- in love.update: server:update()

-- client
client = sock.newClient("127.0.0.1", 22122)
client:connect()
client:on("chat", function(data) print(data.text) end)
-- in love.update: client:update()

docs.title: GameJolt API
docs.text:
Scripts/Libraries/GamejoltAPI.lua wraps the common endpoints of the GameJolt Game API v1.2: users, trophies, sessions, data storage, and score tables.

All requests use HTTPS + MD5 signing and go through the native module Resources/Libs/https.dll.

docs.title: 1. Get the App ID and Private Key
docs.text:
After creating your game on GameJolt, go to the game's Manage → Game API page, where you'll find two things:

Field Description Where to put it game_id The game ID, usually 6–7 digits GamejoltID in Game/conf_pure.lua private_key The private key. Do not let anyone other than the players see it GamejoltPK in Game/conf_pure.lua 
-- Game/conf_pure.lua
Global.SetVariable("GamejoltID", 123456)
Global.SetVariable("GamejoltPK", "abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789")

The two conf_pure.lua files are layered

The one in the root directory holds the engine defaults, and the one in Game/conf_pure.lua overrides it. Put your configuration in Game/conf_pure.lua; see Configuration file.

The private key is baked into the game package

GameJolt's private_key is not "absolutely secret" — it is designed to be distributed with the client (every player's copy contains one). But do not treat it as access control — anyone who unpacks the game can get it. Real write permission relies on username + user_token validation.

docs.title: 2. Initialize (the engine won't do it for you)
docs.text:
Gamejolt.init(Global.GetVariable("GamejoltID"), Global.GetVariable("GamejoltPK"))

init only does three things: converts app_id to a number, stores private_key, and builds base_url.

Source of init 
function gamejolt.init(app_id, private_key)
    gamejolt.app_id = tonumber(app_id)
    gamejolt.private_key = private_key
    gamejolt.base_url = "https://api.gamejolt.com/api/game/v1_2"
    return (gamejolt.app_id ~= nil and gamejolt.private_key ~= nil)
end

You must init first

base_url is only assigned inside init(). If you call fetchUser() and other methods without initializing, URL building will throw an error because it concatenates nil — and it happens when that line runs, not at load time.

docs.title: 3. Check whether it can be used
docs.text:
local ok, err = Gamejolt.isAvailable()
if (not ok) then print(err) end

When the https module cannot be obtained, it returns false and an explanation (which includes the current platform name from SE.system.getOS()).

docs.title: How the signature is computed
docs.text:
Every request must carry a signature parameter, whose value is:

md5.sumhexa(base_url .. request_path .. private_key)

Here request_path is the full path + parameters excluding the signature itself. Each method in the library assembles it itself, so you don't need to worry about it.

generateSignature and apiRequest 
local function generateSignature(request_path)
    local input = gamejolt.base_url .. request_path .. gamejolt.private_key
    return md5.sumhexa(input)
end

local function apiRequest(url)
    if (not https or type(https.request) ~= "function") then
        local platform = (SE and SE.system and SE.system.getOS and SE.system.getOS()) or "Unknown"
        local reason = https_error or "missing native https module"
        return false, "GameJolt API unavailable on "..tostring(platform)..": "..reason
    end

    -- lua-https (https.dll) API: returns code, body, headers
    local code, response, headers = https.request(url)

    if (code ~= 200) then
        return false, "HTTP error: "..tostring(code)
    end

    local data, pos, err = json.decode(response)
    if (not data) then
        return false, "JSON decode error: "..tostring(err).."\nResponse: "..tostring(response)
    end

    if (data.response and data.response.success == "false") then
        return false, data.response.message or "API error"
    end

    return data.response
end

docs.title: Unified return-value convention
docs.text:
Situation Returns Success data.response (a table), no second return value Failure false, error message string

So when calling, either check false first, or wrap it yourself like some methods do:

local res, err = Gamejolt.fetchUser(nil, "somebody")
if (res == false) then
    print("failed:", err)
else
    print(res.users[1].username)
end

On success the second return value is also nil — don't treat it as an error code

For example, fetchUser returns only data.response on success, and the second return value is nil. Writing local res, err = ...; if err then ... is safe, but if (not res) then can also misfire when some interface returns an empty table — using res == false uniformly is the safest.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
General

  • init(app_id, private_key) sets app_id / private_key / base_url and returns whether both are non-empty.
  • isAvailable() whether the native https module is ready. On failure the second return value is an explanation with the platform name.
  • isLoggedIn() whether user_token and username are both set (does not validate correctness, see warning below).

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
Users

  • fetchUser(user_id, username) looks up user info; pass either of the two parameters, login not required.
  • authUser(username, user_token) validates the username + token. On success, gamejolt.username / gamejolt.user_token are kept for later interfaces.

isLoggedIn() is still true after authUser fails

The source code stores the username/token first, then sends the request:

function gamejolt.authUser(username, user_token)
    gamejolt.username = username       -- stored first
    gamejolt.user_token = user_token
    ...
    local success, err = apiRequest(url)
    return success ~= false, err
end

On network failure / wrong token it returns false, err, but the two fields have already been written, so isLoggedIn() still returns true, and all subsequent interfaces that need login will request with the wrong token.

Wrap it yourself:

local ok, err = Gamejolt.authUser(name, token)
if (not ok) then
    Gamejolt.username = nil
    Gamejolt.user_token = nil
end

docs.title: Trophies (achievements)
docs.text:
Trophies

  • fetchAchievements(achieved_only) pulls the trophy list; pass true to achieved_only to return only unlocked ones, login required.
  • unlockAchievement(trophy_id) unlocks the specified trophy; trophy_id is the numeric ID assigned when the trophy was created in the GameJolt backend, login required.
local res = Gamejolt.fetchAchievements(true)
if (res ~= false and res.achievements) then
    for _, a in ipairs(res.achievements) do
        print(a.id, a.title, a.achieved)
    end
end

Gamejolt.unlockAchievement(1047)

trophy_id is not an array index

The ID shown in the backend when creating a trophy is a global number (e.g. 1047), not "the nth one". Filling it wrong returns an API error.

docs.title: Sessions (playtime / status)
docs.text:
GameJolt uses this to track "who is playing, and for how long".

Sessions

  • sessionOpen() opens a session once. In manual mode you just call this line yourself.
  • sessionUpdate(interval, status) recommended. Opens a session once and starts the auto heartbeat. interval is in seconds (default 30, minimum 1); status defaults to "active".
  • sessionPing(status) pings manually once, and can switch the status ("active" / "idle").
  • sessionClose() closes the session and stops the auto heartbeat.
  • update(dt) the timer for the auto heartbeat. The engine already calls it every frame inside love.update(dt), so you don't call it again (calling it would double the frequency).
Gamejolt.sessionUpdate(30, "active")
-- afterwards, Gamejolt.update(dt) accumulates dt each frame and auto-pings every 30 seconds

The auto state is stored in Gamejolt._session_auto; you can read it:

Field Description enabled whether the auto heartbeat is on interval interval (seconds) status the currently reported status elapsed seconds accumulated since the last ping last_error the error message from the last ping (set to nil on success)

interval is seconds, not milliseconds

state.elapsed = state.elapsed + dt, and dt is in seconds. Writing 30000 would give a heartbeat every 30000 seconds.

docs.title: Data storage (cloud save / global data)
docs.text:
A simple key-value store.

Data storage

  • dataStore(key, data, user_data) writes.
    • when user_data is true, it is stored under that user (requires login); otherwise it is stored under game global.
  • dataFetch(key, user_data) reads one key.
  • dataFetchAll(user_data) reads all keys.
  • dataDelete(key, user_data) deletes one key.
  • dataGetKeys(user_data) pulls only the key-name list.
-- The player's own save (requires authUser first)
Gamejolt.dataStore("slot1", json.encode(mySave), true)
local res = Gamejolt.dataFetch("slot1", true)
if (res ~= false and res.data) then mySave = json.decode(res.data) end

-- A game-global announcement (no login required)
Gamejolt.dataStore("motd", "Server maintenance today")

key and data are not URL-encoded at all

The source code concatenates raw strings:

local url = gamejolt.base_url .. "/data-store/set/?game_id=" .. gamejolt.app_id ..
            "&key=" .. key .. "&data=" .. data .. ...

If key or data contains &, =, #, spaces, or Chinese characters, the URL will be truncated / misparsed, and since the signature is computed from the assembled string, the server won't match it and returns a signature error directly.

Workarounds:

  • use only [A-Za-z0-9_-] for the key
  • json.encode the data first, then apply your own percent-encoding (or base64) before sending
  • in short, don't put player-entered text in directly

docs.title: Score tables
docs.text:
Score tables

  • fetchScoresLocal(table_id) pulls the top N entries, no login required. If table_id is omitted, it takes the game's main table.
  • fetchScoresGlobal(table_id) requests with username + user_token; the result includes the player's own rank / neighbors, login required.
  • submitScore(score, table_id, sort, extra_data) submits a score. sort is the value used for display; extra_data is extra text (e.g. time used, level).
Gamejolt.submitScore(12345, 535, 12345, "LV19|Genocide")
local res = Gamejolt.fetchScoresLocal(535)
if (res ~= false and res.scores) then
    for _, s in ipairs(res.scores) do print(s.score, s.user) end
end

submitScore does not carry username/token — it submits a guest score

When assembling the URL, username / user_token are not appended (compare fetchScoresGlobal, which does attach them), so even if you have called authUser, the score is submitted as a guest and won't be attached to the player's account.

To submit an authenticated score, write your own credentialed version following the library's approach, or modify this library.

docs.title: A complete login flow
docs.text:
-- The scene's load / some one-time initialization point
Gamejolt.init(Global.GetVariable("GamejoltID"), Global.GetVariable("GamejoltPK"))

local function login(name, token)
    local ok, err = Gamejolt.authUser(name, token)
    if (not ok) then
        Gamejolt.username, Gamejolt.user_token = nil, nil
        return false, err
    end

    Gamejolt.sessionUpdate(30, "active")      -- auto heartbeat afterwards

    local res = Gamejolt.fetchAchievements(true)
    if (res ~= false and res.achievements) then
        -- sync local achievement state
    end
    return true
end

docs.title: Pitfall summary
docs.text:
All requests are synchronously blocking

https.request(url) blocks until the server responds. Connecting to GameJolt from within China is usually a few hundred milliseconds to a few seconds, and the whole game is frozen for that frame.

  • Never send a request every frame inside love.update
  • One-off requests are acceptable (e.g. a brief freeze when submitting a score)
  • If you want non-blocking behavior you must set up coroutines / threads yourself; the library provides no async version

Failures don't throw — they only return false

If you don't check the return value, failures are silently ignored. All calls are recommended to be written as if (res == false) then ....

The success returned by GameJolt is a string

The library checks data.response.success == "false" — note it is the string "false", not a boolean. This follows the actual return of the GameJolt API, so don't "fix" it.

Unavailable directly on non-Windows platforms

https.dll is a Windows dynamic library. isAvailable() returns false, and all requests return the unified unavailable message. When packaging for Android, it's safest to wrap GameJolt-related logic in if Gamejolt.isAvailable() then.

app_id is converted to a number

gamejolt.app_id = tonumber(app_id). Passing the string "123456" works, but don't pass a value with spaces or letters.

docs.title: Discord RPC
docs.text:
Scripts/Libraries/DiscordRPC.lua makes the Player's Discord profile show "Playing XX" — that is Rich Presence:

SoulEngine
Fighting Sans
Route: Genocide
Played for 12 minutes

Small icons, lobby player count, join buttons, etc. all come from this single library.

docs.title: Why discord-rpc instead of the Game SDK
docs.text:
The comment at the top of the file is very clear; restated here because you should not "upgrade" it:

DiscordRPC.lua:12-18

Why not the Discord Game SDK (discord_game_sdk.dll)? The Game SDK proved unstable / unusable through a direct LuaJIT FFI binding: DiscordCreate succeeds, but get_activity_manager() etc. return NULL no matter what (any flags/version/app-id), so calling any activity method dereferences a NULL pointer and hard-crashes the game.

In other words: the Discord Game SDK crashes the game outright through FFI (it gets a NULL manager pointer), whereas the old discord-rpc library has only a few flat C functions (Discord_Initialize / Discord_UpdatePresence), with no vtable and no manager getter — the path proven to work in LÖVE.

The DiscordGameSDK directory isn't empty, it's just unused

This directory was not deleted; its x64/ and x86/ subdirectories contain 7 files (discord_game_sdk.dll / .dll.lib / .so / .dylib / .bundle), all still under version control.

They remain only as traces of "someone tried this path before" — the engine code references none of them. The one actually loaded is Resources/Libs/DiscordRPC/discord-rpc-x64.dll next door. Don't change the code to call the Game SDK just because they're there — the crash described above was measured.

docs.title: Dependencies and availability conditions
docs.text:
Condition Description LuaJIT's ffi Only present in LÖVE's LuaJIT build. In a pure Lua build the whole library degrades to a no-op Native library files Resources/Libs/DiscordRPC/discord-rpc-x64.dll / discord-rpc-x86.dll Discord client running If Discord isn't open it just won't show, but won't error

Only the Windows library exists for now

Under Resources/Libs/DiscordRPC/ there are only two .dlls, no Linux .so, and no macOS .dylib. Although the source code has the candidate filenames for those two platforms written out, the files are not shipped with the engine. To support other platforms you must download from discord-rpc releases and put them in that directory.

Behavior when dependencies are missing: no error.

local ok, err = Discord.init()
if (not ok) then print(err) end   -- just prints a line, the game keeps running

Without ffi, init / setActivity / on* are all replaced with the same unavailable(), returning false, "DiscordRPC: LuaJIT FFI is unavailable..."; update / shutdown / isAvailable become safe empty functions.

docs.title: The engine already wires it up
docs.text:
main.lua has already run the whole flow:

-- love.load()
Discord.application_id = Global.GetVariable("DiscordAppID")
Discord.init()

Discord.setActivity({
    details     = "Fighting Sans",
    state       = "Route: Genocide",
    large_image = "qq20250220-225345",
    large_text  = "It's a bad time.",
    start       = Discord.timestamp(),   -- timestamp to start counting
})

-- love.update(dt)
Discord.update(dt)

-- love.quit()
Discord.shutdown()

So the most common usage is only one step: replace the ID in Game/conf_pure.lua with your own.

Global.SetVariable("DiscordAppID", "1234567890123456789")

Write it in Game/conf_pure.lua, not the root one

There are two conf_pure.lua files and they are layered: the root one holds engine defaults, and the Game/conf_pure.lua one overrides it. Your changes should go in Game/conf_pure.lua — editing the root one will be overwritten on engine update. For a comparison of the two, see Configuration file.

App ID must be a string

A 19-digit number exceeds 2^53; Lua's number is a double, so writing it as a numeric literal loses precision and Discord will reject the connection.

Global.SetVariable("DiscordAppID", "1342517648348680202")   -- correct
Global.SetVariable("DiscordAppID", 1342517648348680202)     -- wrong: precision loss

The library internally does tostring(client_id), but the precision is already lost at the moment you write it into the config.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Lifecycle

  • init(client_id, options) connects to Discord. If client_id is omitted, it uses Discord.application_id.
    • options.auto_register tries to register the protocol when true (usually not needed).
    • options.steam_id links Steam (optional).
  • update(dt) must be called every frame; internally runs Discord_RunCallbacks(). The engine already calls it inside love.update(dt).
  • shutdown() disconnects, called inside love.quit() (already done by the engine).
  • isAvailable() whether it has been initialized successfully.

Setting Presence

  • setActivity(activity) sets/updates the displayed content; the parameter is a table (fields below).
  • clearActivity() clears the display (the Player returns to the "playing nothing" state).
  • timestamp(seconds) gets the current unix timestamp (seconds); an offset can be passed, used for start / finish.

Callbacks

  • onReady(callback) fires when Discord accepts the connection; the callback receives a user table (userId / username / discriminator / avatar) or nil.
  • onDisconnected(callback) fires on disconnect; the callback receives (errorCode, message).
  • onError(callback) fires on error; the callback receives (errorCode, message). A wrong App ID usually shows up here.
  • onJoin(callback) fires when someone joins via an invite; the callback receives a joinSecret string.
  • onSpectate(callback) fires on spectating; the callback receives a spectateSecret string.
  • onJoinRequest(callback) fires when someone requests to join; the callback receives a user table.
  • respond(user_id, reply) responds to a join request; reply takes Discord.JoinReply.No / .Yes / .Ignore.

Constants and state

  • Discord.JoinReply = { No = 0, Yes = 1, Ignore = 2 }.
  • Discord.VERSION the library version, currently "2.1.0".
  • Discord.application_id your App ID (string).
  • Discord.available whether it has been initialized.
  • Discord.last_error the reason for the most recent failure.

docs.title: What can go in the activity table
docs.text:
Both naming styles are accepted, prefer the underscore column (Game SDK style):

Field Equivalent Meaning Byte limit details — first line of text ("Fighting Sans") 128 state — second line of text ("Route: Genocide") 128 start startTimestamp start timestamp → shows "played xx:xx" — finish / end endTimestamp end timestamp → shows "remaining xx:xx" — large_image largeImageKey large image asset key 32 large_text largeImageText text shown when hovering the large image 128 small_image smallImageKey small image (overlaid on bottom-right of large image) asset key 32 small_text smallImageText text shown when hovering the small image 128 party_id partyId party/room identifier 128 party_size — pass {current count, limit} or {current=, max=} — partySize / partyMax — give the two numbers directly (takes effect when party_size is not used) — match_secret matchSecret match secret 128 join_secret joinSecret secret for invite-join 128 spectate_secret spectateSecret spectate secret 128 instance — whether it can be joined, defaults to true — 
Discord.setActivity({
    details     = "Exploring the ruins",
    state       = "LV " .. DATA.player.lv .. " · HP " .. DATA.player.hp,
    large_image = "ruins",
    large_text  = "Ruins",
    small_image = "frisk",
    small_text  = "Frisk",
    start       = Discord.timestamp(),      -- count from now
    party_size  = {2, 4},                   -- shows (2 of 4)
})

The byte limit is not a character limit

state / details are 128 bytes; under UTF-8 one Chinese character takes 3 bytes — at most about 42 Chinese characters; exceeding it causes Discord to silently drop the whole Presence. Truncate long text yourself.

Image keys must be uploaded in the backend

large_image / small_image holds the key obtained after uploading an image in Discord Developer Portal → your app → Rich Presence → Art Assets (filename without extension), not a file path and not a URL. A key that was never uploaded will silently not show the image. The engine default qq20250220-225345 is an asset under SoulEngine's own app — once you switch to your own App ID it no longer exists, so remember to change it too.

start / finish are second-level unix timestamps

Discord.timestamp() returns os.time(). Passing milliseconds would be treated as the year 50000, and the timer display would break.

docs.title: Three practical usages
docs.text:
① Switch Presence with the scene

function SceneBattle:load()
    Discord.setActivity({
        details = "Fighting " .. Battle.enemies[1].name,
        state   = "LV " .. DATA.player.lv,
        start   = Discord.timestamp(),
    })
end

② Use onReady to confirm the App ID is correct

Discord.onReady(function(user)
    if (user) then
        print("[Discord] connected:", user.username)
    else
        print("[Discord] connected (no user info obtained)")
    end
end)

Discord.onError(function(code, msg)
    print("[Discord] error", code, msg)   -- most likely the App ID is wrong
end)

③ Invite a friend to join

-- host
Discord.setActivity({ ..., party_id = room.id, party_size = {n, 4}, join_secret = room.secret })

-- host receives the request
Discord.onJoinRequest(function(user)
    -- decide for yourself whether to let them in
    Discord.respond(user.userId, Discord.JoinReply.Yes)
end)

docs.title: Pitfall summary
docs.text:
Discord.update(dt) must be called every frame

Internally it is Discord_RunCallbacks(). If you skip it: Presence won't refresh and all callbacks won't fire. The engine already calls it inside love.update(dt); unless you built your own separate love.update branch, don't duplicate it or delete it.

Don't touch that jit.off(discord.update) line

Discord_RunCallbacks() re-enters Lua through the FFI callback from C. Doing this inside JIT-compiled code, LuaJIT throws unprotected error in call to Lua API — and it happens about 2 seconds after connecting to Discord, at the moment the ready event fires. The library specifically turns off JIT for update so it always runs in the interpreter: deleting this line will crash the game when you least expect it.

That comment and code 
-- CRITICAL for LuaJIT: `discord.update` calls Discord_RunCallbacks, which
-- re-enters Lua through the FFI callback trampolines above. ... Disable JIT
-- for this function so it always runs in the interpreter. NOTE: `jit` is a
-- LuaJIT builtin that must be loaded explicitly; the previous
-- `local jit = nil` shadowed the global and silently broke this.
local ok_jit, jit = pcall(require, "jit")
if (ok_jit and jit and jit.off) then
    jit.off(discord.update)
end

Presence has an update rate limit

The Discord server rate-limits (roughly 5 times / 20 seconds); exceeding it silently drops updates and may trigger onError. Don't call setActivity every frame — only call it when the state actually changes (switch scene, level up, enter Battle).

Connecting takes one or two seconds

init() returning true only means the local call succeeded, not that Discord has accepted it. To confirm, hook onReady; Presence generally appears in the client 1–2 seconds later.

Exceptions in callbacks don't crash the game

When a user writes wrong code in a callback, the library catches it with pcall and prints [DiscordRPC] callback error: .... Because these callbacks come in from the C side, a normal pcall can't catch them, so the library wraps one layer in each proxy itself.

instance is on by default

p.instance = (t.instance ~= false) and 1 or 0 — only explicitly writing instance = false turns it off. If join_secret isn't configured, leaving it on does nothing; no invite button appears out of nowhere.

docs.title: sock networking
docs.text:
Scripts/Libraries/Network/sock.lua is a copy of sock.lua v0.3.0, wrapping an event-name + data-table interface on top of ENet (built into LÖVE, reliable UDP):

client:send("playerMove", { x = 100, y = 200 })
-- the other end
server:on("playerMove", function(data, client) ... end)

You don't unpack packets yourself, don't worry about serialization, and don't touch enet's peer/channel details.

There are also two serialization libraries in the same directory; sock picks one to use:

File Description Scripts/Libraries/Network/bitser.lua the one sock uses by default (Robin Wellner's bitser) Scripts/Libraries/Network/binser.lua another similarly named library (Calvin Rose's binser); sock does not auto-load it

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
local sock = ImportFile("Network.sock")

The line that imports enet leaks a global variable

Line 37 of sock.lua reads enet = require "enet" — no local. After loading, _G.enet will be set. This is just namespace pollution and harmless functionally, but if you also use the name enet elsewhere, be careful not to conflict.

docs.title: Two roles
docs.text:
Create Per frame Send message Server sock.newServer(address, port, ...) server:update() sendToAll / sendToAllBut / sendToPeer Client sock.newClient(address, port, ...) client:update() send

newServer

sock.newServer(address, port, maxPeers, maxChannels, inBandwidth, outBandwidth)

  • address the address to bind, defaults to "localhost". To accept LAN / external connections you must pass "*".
  • port the port, defaults to 22122.
  • maxPeers max number of connections, defaults to 64.
  • maxChannels number of channels, defaults to 1.
  • inBandwidth / outBandwidth bandwidth limit (bytes/second), defaults to 0 = unlimited.

newClient

sock.newClient(serverOrAddress, port, maxChannels)

  • Common usage: sock.newClient("127.0.0.1", 22122).
  • Second usage: pass an enet peer, and use it directly as an existing connection (the server internally builds client objects this way).

Both ends' maxChannels must match

ENet requires the client and server to have the same number of channels. The default is 1, meaning if you want multiple channels, both sides must explicitly pass the same number, otherwise they can't connect.

A used port will directly error()

if not server.host then
